value.zh: 鄭倜劫苗英降，英不從，殺之，攜其首以降，於是士卒大潰。
value.en: Zheng Tong tried to force Miao Ying to surrender. Ying refused and was killed. Tong carried Ying's head to the Mongols and surrendered, and the army collapsed in rout.
value.literal: Zheng Tong seized Miao Ying to force his surrender; Ying refused and was killed. Tong carried his head to surrender, and then the soldiers collapsed in great rout.

value.zh: 兀典、合閏提數十騎走山間，追騎禽得，皆殺之。
value.en: Wudian and Hehun fled through the mountains with several dozen horsemen. Pursuers overtook and captured them, and both were executed.
value.literal: Wudian and Hehun took several dozen horsemen and fled through the mountains; pursuing riders captured them and all were killed.

value.zh: 先是，兀典嘗為鄧州節度使，世襲謀克黃摑三合時為宣差都總領，與兀典親厚，故決計入鄧。
value.en: Wudian had previously served as military commissioner of Dengzhou. The hereditary commander Huangzha Sanheshi, then imperial commissioner and overall chief, was on close terms with him, which is why the army resolved to march toward Deng.
value.literal: Earlier, Wudian had once been military commissioner of Dengzhou; the hereditary commander Huangzha Sanheshi was imperial commissioner and overall chief, on intimate terms with Wudian, and therefore the decision was made to enter Deng.

value.zh: 是役也，安平、蕩寇、鷹揚、振威諸都尉，及西安、金雞等軍，脫走者百才一二。
value.en: Of the Anping, Bandit-Suppression, Eagle Soar, and Zhenwei commandants and the Xi'an, Golden Rooster, and other units, scarcely one or two in a hundred escaped.
value.literal: In this campaign, of the Anping, Bandit-Suppression, Eagle Soar, and Zhenwei commandants, and the Xi'an, Golden Rooster, and other forces, only one or two in a hundred escaped.

value.zh: 列傳第六十六 循吏 ○盧克忠 牛德昌 范承吉 王政 張奕 李瞻 劉敏行 傅慎微 劉煥 高昌福 孫德淵 趙鑒 蒲察鄭留 女奚烈守愚 石抹元 張彀 趙重福 武都 紇石烈德 張特立 王浩

value.zh: 宣皇帝諱懿，字仲達，河內溫縣孝敬里人，姓司馬氏。
value.en: Emperor Xuan had the personal name Yi and the courtesy name Zhongda. He came from Xiaojing Ward in Wen County, Henei Commandery, and belonged to the Sima clan.
value.literal: Emperor Xuan's taboo name was Yi; his courtesy name was Zhongda. He was a native of Xiaojing Ward in Wen County in Henei, and his surname was Sima.

value.zh: 其先出自帝高陽之子重黎，為夏官祝融。
value.en: The line descended from Chongli, son of Zhuanxu, who served as Zhurong under the ancient office of Xia.
value.literal: His ancestors traced their line to Chongli, son of Emperor Gaoyang (Zhuanxu), who held the office of Zhurong under the Xia.

value.zh: 歷唐、虞、夏、商，世序其職。
value.en: Across Tang, Yu, Xia, and Shang, his forebears held that post in unbroken succession.
value.literal: Through the eras of Tang, Yu, Xia, and Shang, generation after generation they succeeded one another in that office.

value.zh: 及周，以夏官為司馬。
value.en: Under the Zhou, the old Xia office became the office of Sima, the marshal.
value.literal: Under the Zhou, the Xia ministry was styled Marshal (Sima).

value.zh: 其後程伯休父，周宣王時，以世官克平徐方，錫以官族，因而為氏。
value.en: Later, Cheng Bo Xiufu—during King Xuan of Zhou—used his hereditary charge to crush the Xu region and received a clan designation from his title; from that the Sima surname arose.
value.literal: Later Cheng Bo Xiufu, in the reign of King Xuan of Zhou, by virtue of his hereditary office conquered and pacified the Xu lands and was granted a clan name taken from his office; his descendants therefore took Sima as their surname.

value.zh: 楚漢間，司馬卬為趙將，與諸侯伐秦。
value.en: In the turmoil between Chu and Han, Sima Ang commanded troops for Zhao and marched with the alliance against Qin.
value.literal: Between Chu and Han, Sima Ang served as a Zhao general and joined the feudal lords in attacking Qin.

value.zh: 秦亡，立為殷王，都河內。
value.en: After Qin collapsed he was enthroned as king of Yin with his seat at Henei.
value.literal: When Qin fell, [Ang] was established as King of Yin and made his capital in Henei.

value.zh: 漢以其地為郡，子孫遂家焉。
value.en: The Han turned that territory into a commandery, and his line took root there.
value.literal: Han converted his territory into a commandery, and his descendants settled there.

value.zh: 自卬八世，生征西將軍鈞，字叔平。
value.en: Eight generations down from Ang came General Who Guards the West Jun, whose courtesy name was Shuping.
value.literal: Eight generations after Ang was born General Who Guards the West Jun, courtesy name Shuping.

value.zh: 鈞生豫章太守量，字公度。
value.en: Jun’s son was Liang, prefect of Yuzhang, courtesy name Gongdu.
value.literal: Jun fathered Prefect of Yuzhang Liang, courtesy name Gongdu.

value.zh: 量生潁川太守儁，字元異。
value.en: Liang’s son was Jun, prefect of Yingchuan, courtesy name Yuanyi.
value.literal: Liang fathered Prefect of Yingchuan Jun, courtesy name Yuanyi.

value.zh: 儁生京兆尹防，字建公。
value.en: Jun’s son was Fang, governor of Jingzhao, courtesy name Jiangong.
value.literal: Jun fathered Governor of the Metropolitan Region Fang, courtesy name Jiangong.

value.zh: 帝即防之第二子也。
value.en: He was the second son of Fang.
value.literal: The Emperor was Fang’s second son.

value.zh: 少有奇節，聰朗多大略，博學洽聞，伏膺儒教。
value.en: Even young he revealed unusual steadfastness—acute, far-sighted, erudite, and steeped in the Confucian canon.
value.literal: In youth he showed uncommon integrity; he was bright and broad in strategic grasp, widely read and well informed, and devoted himself to Confucian teaching.

value.zh: 漢末大亂，常慨然有憂天下心。
value.en: As Han unraveled, he was repeatedly consumed by anxiety for the empire.
value.literal: At the end of Han, when great turmoil arose, he often felt stirred with concern for the realm.

value.zh: 南陽太守同郡楊俊名知人，[1]見帝，未弱冠，以為非常之器。
value.en: Yang Jun of Nanyang—his fellow townsman and a celebrated judge of talent—met him before his cap-and-girdle ceremony and pronounced him a figure of rare promise.
value.literal: Yang Jun of the same commandery, prefect of Nanyang, famed for judging men,[1] met the Emperor before his twentieth year and deemed him an extraordinary vessel.

value.zh: 尚書清河崔琰與帝兄朗善，亦謂朗曰：「君弟聰亮明允，剛斷英特，非子所及也。」
value.en: Cui Yan of Qinghe, who served in the Secretariat, was close to his elder brother Sima Lang and told Lang, “Your brother combines lucidity with integrity and carries an iron decisiveness—you cannot rival him.”
value.literal: Minister Cui Yan of Qinghe was on good terms with the Emperor’s elder brother Lang and also said to Lang, “Your younger brother is clear-sighted and fair-minded, resolute and extraordinary—not someone you can match.”

value.zh: 武都氐王苻雙強端帥其屬六千餘人來降 據蜀志張嶷傳、華陽國志七，武都氐王苻健降蜀，其弟率眾就魏。
value.en: According to the Shu zhi biography of Zhang Yi and Huayang guozhi 7, the Jinshu names Fu Shuang and Qiang Duan as Wudu Di kings leading more than six thousand followers to surrender; those sources instead have Wudu Di king Fu Jian surrender to Shu while his younger brother led a host to Wei.
value.literal: Di kings of Wudu Fu Shuang and Qiang Duān leading followers—according to Shu Records Zhang Yi biography and Huayang guozhi 7 Wudu Di king Fu Jian surrendered to Shu while his younger brother led crowds to Wei.

value.zh: 苻雙並非氐王，疑「王」字衍。
value.en: Fu Shuang was not a Di king, so the graph "king" is suspected to be intrusive.
value.literal: Fu Shuang was not a Di king, so the graph "king" is suspected to be intrusive.

value.zh: 景皇帝諱師，字子元，宣帝長子也。
value.en: Emperor Jing, whose personal name was Shi and courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan of Jin.
value.literal: Emperor Jing, taboo name Shi, courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan.

value.zh: 雅有風彩，沈毅多大略。
value.en: He carried himself with quiet distinction, steady and resolute, with a strategist’s breadth of mind.
value.literal: He had refined bearing and presence, was deep and resolute, and possessed great strategic vision.

value.zh: 少流美譽，與夏侯玄、何晏齊名。
value.en: While still young he was widely praised, and his name stood alongside those of Xiahou Xuan and He Yan.
value.literal: In youth he enjoyed a fine reputation, and was ranked with Xiahou Xuan and He Yan.

value.zh: 晏常稱曰：「惟幾也能成天下之務，司馬子元是也。」
value.en: He Yan used to say, "It takes someone who senses the moment before it turns to carry the weight of the realm—and that man is Sima Ziyuan."
value.literal: He Yan often declared, "Only one who apprehends subtle turning points can accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven; Sima Ziyuan is such a man."

value.zh: 魏景初中，拜散騎常侍，累遷中護軍。
value.en: During Wei’s Jingchu years he received appointment as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and rose step by step to Central Protector of the Army.
value.literal: In the Jingchu era of Wei, he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and eventually promoted to Central Protector of the Army.

value.zh: 為選用之法，舉不越功，吏無私焉。
value.en: He set rules for appointments so that promotions matched real achievement, and his staff could not trade on personal connections.
value.literal: He established methods for selection and appointment; recommendations did not exceed actual merit, and clerks practiced no private favoritism.

value.zh: 宣穆皇后崩，居喪以至孝聞。
value.en: After Empress Dowager Xuanmu’s death, he kept mourning with such scrupulous grief that word of his filial piety spread everywhere.
value.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuanmu died, he observed mourning for her and was famed for extreme filial devotion.

value.zh: 宣帝之將誅曹爽，深謀秘策，獨與帝潛畫，文帝弗之知也。
value.en: As Sima Yi readied the strike against Cao Shuang, he laid his plans in the deepest secrecy—working them out alone with Sima Shi—while Sima Zhao was kept entirely in the dark.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan was about to execute Cao Shuang, with deep plots and secret stratagems he secretly planned only with the Emperor (Sima Shi); Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao) did not know of it.

value.zh: 將發夕乃告之，既而使人覘之，帝寢如常，而文帝不能安席。
value.en: Sima Yi waited until the night before the coup to inform his son; when he sent men to watch Sima Shi’s quarters, Shi slept soundly as on any other night, while Sima Zhao tossed and could not settle.
value.literal: On the eve of launching the action he was told; then someone was sent to spy on him—the Emperor slept as usual, but Emperor Wen could not find rest on his mat.

value.zh: 晨會兵司馬門，鎮靜內外，置陣甚整。
value.en: At daybreak he drew up his forces at the Sima Gate, steadying the palace inside and out and arraying them with flawless discipline.
value.literal: At dawn he assembled troops at the Sima Gate, calming inside and outside, and deployed formations in very good order.

value.zh: 宣帝曰：「此子竟可也。」
value.en: Sima Yi said, "This boy will do after all."
value.literal: Emperor Xuan said, "This son is indeed capable."

value.zh: 初，帝陰養死士三千，散在人間，至是一朝而集，眾莫知所出也。
value.en: Earlier, Sima Shi had quietly kept three thousand devoted fighters dispersed through the capital; now they materialized overnight, and no one could guess where they had sprung from.
value.literal: At the outset the Emperor had secretly maintained three thousand bravos, scattered among the people; at this moment they gathered in a single morning, and the multitude did not know whence they had come.

value.zh: 事平，以功封長平鄉侯，食邑千戶，尋加衛將軍。
value.en: After the coup succeeded he was rewarded with the village marquisate of Changping and a thousand-household fief, and before long was named General of the Guard as well.
value.literal: When the affair was settled, by merit he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Changping with a fief of one thousand households; soon he was additionally appointed General of the Guard.

value.zh: 及宣帝薨，議者咸云「伊尹既卒，伊陟嗣事」，天子命帝以撫軍大將軍輔政。
value.en: At Sima Yi’s death, court opinion echoed the old line—“When Yi Yin passed away, his son Yi Zhi carried on the task”—and the Wei emperor appointed Sima Shi General Who Pacifies the Army to assist in government.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, those who deliberated all said, "After Yi Yin died, Yi Zhi succeeded to his duties," and the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor as General Who Stabilizes the Army and Great General to assist in government.

value.zh: 魏嘉平四年春正月，遷大將軍，加侍中，持節、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事。
value.en: In the first month of spring, Wei’s fourth year of Jiaping, he advanced to Great General, was given the concurrent post of Palace Attendant, received the imperial baton, took overall command of central and frontier forces, and assumed control of the Secretariat.
value.literal: In the first month of spring in the fourth year of Jiaping of Wei, he was promoted to Great General, added as Palace Attendant, bearing credentials, supervising all military affairs of the central command and the regions, and recording Director of the Secretariat business.

value.zh: 命百官舉賢才，明少長，恤窮獨，理廢滯。
value.en: He instructed every office to put forward able men, to sort seniority fairly, to relieve the widowed and alone, and to clear the backlog of neglected business.
value.literal: He ordered the hundred officials to recommend worthy talent, clarify precedence of young and old, show pity to the destitute and solitary, and straighten out stalled appointments.

value.zh: 諸葛誕、毌丘儉、王昶、陳泰、胡遵都督四方，王基、州泰、鄧艾、石苞典州郡，盧毓、李豐裳選舉，傅嘏、虞松參計謀，鐘會、夏侯玄、王肅、陳本、孟康、趙酆、張緝預朝議，四海傾注，朝野肅然。
value.en: Zhuge Dan, Guanqiu Jian, Wang Chang, Chen Tai, and Hu Zun held regional commands; Wang Ji, Zhou Tai, Deng Ai, and Shi Bao ran the provinces; Lu Yu and Li Feng handled personnel; Fu Gu and Yu Song shaped policy; Zhong Hui, Xiahou Xuan, Wang Su, Chen Ben, Meng Kang, Zhao Feng, and Zhang Ji sat in on the great councils. The empire fixed its hopes on them, and court and countryside grew solemn.
value.literal: Zhuge Dan, Guanqiu Jian, Wang Chang, Chen Tai, and Hu Zun supervised the four quarters; Wang Ji, Zhou Tai, Deng Ai, and Shi Bao administered prefectures and commanderies; Lu Yu and Li Feng oversaw selection and appointment; Fu Gu and Yu Song joined in planning stratagems; Zhong Hui, Xiahou Xuan, Wang Su, Chen Ben, Meng Kang, Zhao Feng, and Zhang Ji took part in court deliberations; the four seas turned their gaze upon them, and court and countryside stood in solemn awe.

value.zh: 或有請改易制度者，帝曰：「'不識不知，順帝之則'，詩人之美也。
value.en: When voices rose for sweeping institutional change, Sima Shi answered, "The Odes praise the ruler who does not meddle for show but simply follows the pattern Heaven set for the sage-kings.
value.literal: When some requested changes to institutions, the Emperor said: "'Not knowing, not perceiving, following the norms of the Di'—that is what the poets praise.

value.zh: 三祖典制，所宜遵奉；
value.en: The precedents left by the three Wei founders are what we are bound to honor;
value.literal: The regulations of the three founding ancestors are what ought to be obeyed and upheld;

value.zh: 自非軍事，不得妄有改革。」
value.en: and apart from what war demands, nothing should be changed on a whim."
value.literal: unless it be military affairs, one must not recklessly carry out reforms."

value.zh: 四年春二月丁丑，天子復命帝如前，又固讓。
value.en: On dingchou in the second month of spring, the fourth year, the emperor repeated the old honors; Sima Zhao refused again.
value.literal: Fourth year, spring, second month, day dingchou, the Son of Heaven again ordered the Emperor as before; again firmly declined.

value.zh: 三月，詔大將軍府增置司馬一人，從事中郎二人，舍人十人。
value.en: In the third month an edict added one major, two retainers, and ten gentlemen to the grand general’s staff.
value.literal: Third month, edict: Great General's mansion additionally establish one Major, two Retainers, ten Gentlemen.

value.zh: 夏，帝將伐蜀，乃謀眾曰：「自定壽春已來，息役六年，治兵繕甲，以擬二虜。
value.en: That summer, as he readied the Shu expedition, he told his council, "Six years have passed since Shouchun fell—six years we have spent forging arms to meet Wu and Shu.
value.literal: Summer, the Emperor was about to campaign against Shu; then he consulted the host saying: "Since settling Shouchun, we have rested corvée six years, drilled troops and repaired armor, in order to target the two bandits.

value.zh: 略計取吳，作戰船，通水道，當用千餘萬功，此十萬人百數十日事也。
value.en: A Wu campaign—building hulls and dredging channels—would swallow ten million man-days; a hundred thousand laborers would need months on end.
value.literal: Roughly calculating taking Wu, building war boats, opening water routes, ought to use more than ten million man-days of work; this is a matter of one hundred several tens of days for one hundred thousand men.

value.zh: 又南土下濕，必生疾疫。
value.en: The southern marshes breed sickness; an army would wilt there.
value.literal: Moreover southern soil is low and damp; surely sickness and pestilence will arise.

value.zh: 今宜先取蜀，三年之後，在巴蜀順流之勢，水陸並進，此滅虞定虢，吞韓並魏之勢也。
value.en: Better to take Shu first; three years later, riding the Yangzi current from Ba and Shu, we can move by water and land together—the old stratagem of swallowing the neighbor to fatten the conqueror.
value.literal: Now it is fitting first to take Shu; after three years, with Ba-Shu's down-current momentum, water and land advancing together—this is the momentum of destroying Yu and settling Guo, swallowing Han and annexing Wei.

value.zh: 計蜀戰士九萬，居守成都及備他郡不下四萬，然則餘眾不過五萬。
value.en: Shu lists ninety thousand troops, but forty thousand must hold Chengdu and the outlying commanderies—no more than fifty thousand can meet us in the field.
value.literal: Calculating Shu warriors ninety thousand; dwelling to guard Chengdu and garrison other commanderies not less than forty thousand; then the remaining host does not exceed fifty thousand.

value.zh: 今絆姜維於遝中，使不得東顧，直指駱穀，出其空虛之地，以襲漢中。
value.en: Pin Jiang Wei in Taozhong so he cannot shift east, then drive straight through Luogu into the empty heart of Hanzhong.
value.literal: Now pin Jiang Wei in Taozhong, causing him not to be able to look east; point straight to Luogu Valley, emerge in their empty hollow ground, to raid Hanzhong.

value.zh: 彼若嬰城守險，兵勢必散，首尾離絕。
value.en: If they hug the walls and cling to the defiles, their strength will splinter and van detach from van.
value.literal: If they gird the city and guard the peril, military momentum must scatter; head and tail are cut off.

value.zh: 舉大眾以屠城，散銳卒以略野，劍閣不暇守險，關頭不能自存。
value.en: Mass the army to storm the towns, send flying columns to scour the open country, and Jiange will have no time to hold the narrows while the Guan passes collapse on their own.
value.literal: Raise a great host to slaughter the city; scatter picked troops to sweep the wilds; Jiange will have no leisure to guard the peril; Guantou cannot preserve itself.

value.zh: 以劉禪之暗，而邊城外破，士女內震，其亡可知也。」
value.en: Liu Shan is a dull tool; once the frontier cracks and panic seizes the capital, his fall is a foregone conclusion."
value.literal: With Liu Shan's darkness, and border cities broken from without, gentlemen and ladies within shaken, its perishing can be known.

value.zh: 征西將軍鄧艾以為未有釁，屢陳異議。
value.en: Deng Ai, the western commander, argued there was no opening yet and kept filing objections.
value.literal: General Who Conquers the West Deng Ai thought there was not yet a crack, repeatedly presented divergent opinions.

value.zh: 帝患之，使主簿師纂為艾司馬以喻之，艾乃奉命。
value.en: Annoyed by Deng Ai’s foot-dragging, Sima Zhao made his chief clerk Shi Zuan Deng Ai’s major to talk sense into him; Deng then accepted the order.
value.literal: The Emperor worried about it, ordered Chief Clerk Shi Zuan to become Ai's Major in order to instruct him; Ai then received the command.

value.zh: 於是征四方之兵十八萬，使鄧艾自狄道攻姜維於遝中，雍州刺史諸葛緒自祁山軍于武街，絕維歸路，鎮西將軍鐘會帥前將軍李輔、征蜀護軍胡烈等自駱穀襲漢中。
value.en: He raised a hundred and eighty thousand men from every quarter: Deng Ai moved from Didao against Jiang Wei in Taozhong; Yongzhou Inspector Zhuge Xu marched from Qishan to Wujie to sever Jiang Wei’s retreat; Zhong Hui, General Who Guards the West, led Li Fu, Hu Lie, and the rest through Luogu against Hanzhong.
value.literal: Thereupon conscripted troops of the four quarters one hundred eighty thousand, ordered Deng Ai from Didao to attack Jiang Wei in Taozhong, Inspector of Yongzhou Zhuge Xu from Qishan to encamp at Wujie, cutting off Jiang Wei's return route, General Who Guards the West Zhong Hui leading Former General Li Fu, Shu Campaign Protector Hu Lie, and others from Luogu Valley to raid Hanzhong.

value.zh: 秋八月，軍發洛陽，大賚將士，陳師誓眾。
value.en: In the eighth month of autumn the host left Luoyang after rich gifts to the ranks, a full review, and oaths to the army.
value.literal: Autumn, eighth month, the army set out from Luoyang, greatly rewarded officers and soldiers, arrayed the host and swore the multitude.

value.zh: 將軍鄧敦謂蜀未可討，帝斬以徇。
value.en: General Deng Dun said Shu was not ripe for attack; Sima Zhao struck off his head as a warning.
value.literal: General Deng Dun said Shu could not be punished; the Emperor beheaded him to display.

value.zh: 九月，又使天水太守王頎攻維營，隴西太守牽弘邀其前，金城太守楊頎趣甘松。
value.en: In the ninth month he sent Tianshui’s Wang Qi against Jiang Wei’s camp, Longxi’s Qian Hong to block his van, and Jincheng’s Yang Qi toward Gansong.
value.literal: Ninth month, again ordered Tianshui Grand Administrator Wang Qi to attack Wei's camp, Longxi Grand Administrator Qian Hong to intercept his front, Jincheng Grand Administrator Yang Qi to hurry to Gansong.

value.zh: 鐘會分為二隊，入自斜谷，使李輔圍王含于樂城，又使步將易愷攻蔣斌于漢城。
value.en: Zhong Hui split his force, entered by Xie Valley, set Li Fu to invest Wang Han at Lecheng, and sent Yi Kai against Jiang Bin at Hancheng.
value.literal: Zhong Hui divided into two columns, entered from Xie Valley, ordered Li Fu to besiege Wang Han at Lecheng, also ordered infantry general Yi Kai to attack Jiang Bin at Hancheng.

value.zh: 會直指陽安，護軍胡烈攻陷關城。
value.en: Zhong Hui drove straight on Yang’an while Protector Hu Lie stormed the pass fort.
value.literal: Hui pointed straight to Yang'an; Protector Hu Lie attacked and took Guancheng.

value.zh: 姜維聞之，引還，王頎追敗維于強川。
value.en: Jiang Wei wheeled about; Wang Qi ran him down at Qiangchuan and broke his column.
value.literal: When Jiang Wei heard it, he led back; Wang Qi pursued and defeated Wei at Qiangchuan.

value.zh: 維與張翼、廖化合軍守劍閣，鐘會攻之。
value.en: Jiang Wei joined Zhang Yi and Liao Hua to hold Jiange; Zhong Hui laid siege.
value.literal: Wei joined Zhang Yi and Liao Hua combining armies to guard Jiange; Zhong Hui attacked it.

value.zh: 冬十月，天子以諸侯獻捷交至，乃申前命曰：
value.en: In the tenth winter month, as victory dispatches from the lords piled in, the emperor renewed his earlier charge, saying:
value.literal: Winter, tenth month, the Son of Heaven because the nobles' presented victories arrived in succession, then reiterated the former command saying:

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
value.en: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
value.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

value.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
value.en: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
value.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

value.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
value.en: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.

value.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
value.en: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
value.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

value.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
value.en: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.

value.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
value.en: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."
value.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."

value.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
value.en: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
value.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

value.zh: 序
value.en: Preface
value.literal: Preface

value.zh: 晉自元康之後，政亂朝昏，禍難薦興，艱虞孔熾，遂使奸凶放命，戎狄交侵，函夏沸騰，蒼生塗炭，干戈日用，戰爭方興。
value.en: After the Yuankang years, Jin fell into turmoil: the administration unraveled and the court grew dim; calamities piled up and distress burned hot. Villains defied authority, northern tribes took turns raiding the heartland, the realm convulsed, and common folk were ground to dust under ceaseless arms and spreading war.
value.literal: From after the Yuankang era of Jin, government was chaotic and the court dark; disasters arose in succession and hardship blazed fiercely, so that villains threw off restraint and Rong and Di invaded in turn; the heartland seethed, the black-haired people were smeared with charcoal; arms were wielded daily and war had just begun to rise.

value.zh: 雖背恩忘義之徒不可勝載，而蹈節輕生之士無乏于時。
value.en: Traitors who threw away obligation were beyond counting, yet men who chose principle over life were never absent in those same years.
value.literal: Though men who betrayed grace and forgot duty could not be fully recorded, yet men who embraced integrity and held life lightly were not lacking in that age.

value.zh: 至若嵇紹之衛難乘輿，卞壼之亡軀鋒鏑，桓雄之義高田叔，周崎之節邁解揚，羅丁致命於舊君，辛吉恥臣於戎虜，張禕引鴆以全節，王諒斷臂以厲忠，莫不志烈秋霜，精貫白日，足以激清風于萬古，厲薄俗于當年者歟！
value.en: Think of Ji Shao guarding the emperor's carriage in peril, Bian Kun falling to blades and shafts, Huan Xiong matching Tian Shu in devotion, Zhou Qi outdoing Jie Yang in steadfastness, Luo Ding dying for a former sovereign, Xin Ji refusing to bow to alien rulers, Zhang Yi drinking poison to keep his honor, Wang Liang cutting off an arm to prove his loyalty—each will like autumn frost, each spirit bright as noon, enough to quicken moral clarity for ages and shame a degenerate age.
value.literal: As for Ji Shao shielding the imperial carriage in crisis, Bian Kun losing his body to spearheads and arrows, Huan Xiong, whose righteousness rivaled Tian Shu, Zhou Qi, whose integrity surpassed Jie Yang, Luo Ding laying down his life for his former lord, Xin Ji ashamed to serve barbarians as minister, Zhang Yi draining poison to preserve his integrity, Wang Liang severing an arm to steel his loyalty—all alike bore wills fierce as autumn frost and spirits piercing as the noon sun, enough to stir pure wind through ten thousand ages and shame shallow ways in their own day!

value.zh: 所謂亂世識忠臣，斯之謂也。
value.en: This is what men mean when they say troubled times reveal who the loyal ministers are.
value.literal: What is called "in troubled times one recognizes loyal ministers" refers to this.

value.zh: 卞壼、劉超、鐘雅、周虓等已入列傳，其餘即敘其行事以為《忠義傳》，用旌晉氏之有人焉。
value.en: Bian Kun, Liu Chao, Zhong Ya, Zhou Xiao, and the like already have full biographies elsewhere; those who remain are collected here under Loyalty and Righteousness to show that the Jin court could still claim men of honor.
value.literal: Bian Kun, Liu Chao, Zhong Ya, Zhou Xiao, and others have already entered the standard biographies; the rest are here narrated in conduct gathered as the "Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness," to signal that the House of Jin still had such men.

value.zh: 苻丕 苻登
value.en: This chapter records Fu Pi and Fu Deng.
value.literal: Fu Pi; Fu Deng.

value.zh: 先是，慕容驎攻王兗於博陵，至是糧竭矢盡，郡功曹張猗逾城聚眾應驎。
value.en: Before this, Murong Lin had been besieging Wang Yan in Boling; supplies and arrows ran out, and Zhang Yi, the county merit clerk, scaled the walls, raised a band of followers, and opened the city to Lin.
value.literal: Earlier, Murong Lin had attacked Wang Yan at Boling; by now grain and arrows were exhausted, and the county merit officer Zhang Yi climbed the wall, gathered a crowd, and went over to Lin.

value.zh: 袞臨城數之曰：「卿，秦之人也。
value.en: Wang Yan appeared on the battlements and cried out, "You were born a subject of Qin.
value.literal: Yan stood on the wall and rebuked him, saying: "You are a man of Qin.

value.zh: 吾，卿之君也。
value.en: I am the lord you serve.
value.literal: I am your lord.

value.zh: 起眾應賊，號稱義兵，何名實相違之甚！
value.en: You rouse the people for the rebels yet name it a loyal host—never was deed and title so at odds!
value.literal: You raised a host to answer the bandit and call it a righteous army—how far name and fact are twisted!

value.zh: 卿兄往合鄉宗，親逐城主，天地不容，為世大戮。
value.en: Your brother once mustered the clan, chased the lawful governor from the walls, and earned the scorn of heaven and earth—a public enemy while he lived.
value.literal: Your elder brother once joined your village kin, personally drove out the city's master; heaven and earth would not shelter him—he became the great criminal of his age.

value.zh: 身滅未幾，卿復續之。
value.en: He has scarcely paid for his crimes in the grave, and you follow in his footsteps.
value.literal: His person was destroyed not long ago, and you have taken up his course.

value.zh: 卿見為吾吏，親尋干戈，競為戎首，為爾君者，不亦難乎！
value.en: You served under my banner, then seized weapons with your own hands and led the alien host—what lord could forgive such a thing?
value.literal: You have been my officer, yet you personally took up arms and strove to be chief among the barbarians—for your lord, is that not hard indeed!

value.zh: 今人何取卿一切之功，寧能忘卿不忠不孝之事！
value.en: Men may praise your little coup today, but they will not forget that you are faithless to your prince and heartless toward your kin!
value.literal: What do men value in your petty moment of glory—can they forget your deeds of disloyalty and unfilial impiety!

value.zh: 古人有雲，求忠臣必出孝子之門，卿母在城，不能顧之，何忠義之可望！
value.en: The old proverb runs that loyal servants come from filial homes; your mother is trapped in this town while you betray it—where is your duty or your honor?
value.literal: The ancients said, seek loyal ministers among the households of filial sons; your mother is inside the city and you do not care for her—what loyalty or righteousness can be expected!

value.zh: 惡不絕世，卿之謂也。
value.en: They say wickedness outlives a single life—you prove the saying.
value.literal: Evil does not die with the generation—this is said of you.

value.zh: 不圖中州禮義之邦邦，而卿門風若斯。
value.en: I never thought to see, in the heartland where rites and duty are taught, a family sink to such conduct as yours.
value.literal: I did not expect that in the Central Plains, the land of ritual and propriety, the conduct of your clan should be thus.

value.zh: 卿去老母如脫屣，吾復何論哉！」
value.en: You abandoned your old mother like a pair of worn-out sandals—I have nothing left to say to you!"
value.literal: You cast off your aged mother as one casts off worn shoes—what more is there for me to say!"

value.zh: 既而城陷，兗及固安侯苻鑒，並為驎所殺。
value.en: The city soon fell; Wang Yan and Fu Jian, marquis of Gu'an, were both slain by Murong Lin.
value.literal: Soon the city fell; Yan and the Marquis of Gu'an Fu Jian were both killed by Lin.

value.zh: 王及善，洺州邯鄲人也。
value.en: Wang Jishan was a native of Handan in Mozhou.
value.literal: Wang Jishan was a native of Handan in Mozhou.

value.zh: 父君愕。
value.en: His father was Jun'e.
value.literal: His father was Jun'e.

value.zh: 隋大業末，并州人王君廓掠邯鄲，君愕往說君廓曰：「方今萬乘失禦，英雄競起，誠宜撫納遺氓，保全形勝，按甲以觀時變，擁眾而歸真主，此富貴可圖也。
value.en: At the end of the Sui Emperor Yang's reign, Wang Junguo of Bingzhou raided Handan. Jun'e went to persuade Junguo, saying, "At present the throne has lost its guidance and heroes are rising in rivalry. You truly ought to win over the scattered populace, secure your strategic strongholds, hold your forces in check to observe how affairs change, gather followers and return them to the true sovereign — then wealth and honor can be pursued.
value.literal: At the end of the Sui Emperor Yang's reign, Wang Junguo of Bingzhou raided Handan. Jun'e went to persuade Junguo, saying, "At present the imperial throne has lost its guidance and heroes are rising in rivalry. You truly ought to win over the scattered populace, secure your strategic strongholds, hold your forces in check to observe how affairs change, gather followers and return them to the true sovereign — then wealth and honor can be pursued.

value.zh: 今足下居無尺土之地，守無兼旬之糧，恣行殘忍，所過攘奪，竊爲足下寒心矣。」
value.en: Now you possess not a foot of territory, nor food enough for even ten days. You indulge in cruelty wherever you go and plunder as you pass. I fear for you on your account."
value.literal: Now you possess not a foot of territory, nor food enough for even ten days. You indulge in cruelty wherever you go and plunder as you pass. I fear for you on your account."

value.zh: 君廓曰：「計將安出？」
value.en: Junguo said, "What plan do you propose?"
value.literal: Junguo said, "What plan do you propose?"

value.zh: 君愕爲陳井陘之險，可先往據之。
value.en: Jun'e explained the strategic advantages of Jingxing Pass and advised that he go there first to seize it.
value.literal: Jun'e explained the strategic advantages of Jingxing Pass and advised that he go there first to seize it.

value.zh: 君廓從其言，乃屯井陘山。
value.en: Junguo followed his advice and encamped on Mount Jingxing.
value.literal: Junguo followed his advice and encamped on Mount Jingxing.

value.zh: 歲餘，會義師入定關中，乃與君廓率所部萬餘人來降，拜大將軍。
value.en: After more than a year, when the righteous army entered and pacified Guanzhong, he and Junguo led their more than ten thousand followers to surrender and were appointed Grand General.
value.literal: After more than a year, when the righteous army entered and pacified Guanzhong, he and Junguo led their more than ten thousand followers to surrender and were appointed Grand General.

value.zh: 頻以戰功封新興縣公，累遷左武衛將軍。
value.en: For repeated military achievements he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xinxing County and was promoted in succession to General of the Left Martial Guards.
value.literal: Repeatedly for military achievements he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xinxing County and was promoted in succession to General of the Left Martial Guards.

value.zh: 從太宗征遼東，兼領左屯營兵馬。
value.en: When he followed Emperor Taizong on the campaign against Liaodong, he also commanded the troops of the Left Encampment.
value.literal: When he followed Emperor Taizong on the campaign against Liaodong, he also commanded the troops of the Left Encampment.

value.zh: 與高麗戰於駐蹕山，君愕先鋒陷陣，力戰而死。
value.en: Fighting the Goguryeo at Mount Zhubi, Jun'e led the vanguard in breaking the enemy lines and died fighting fiercely.
value.literal: Fighting the Goguryeo at Mount Zhubi, Jun'e led the vanguard in breaking the enemy lines and died fighting fiercely.

value.zh: 太宗深痛悼之，贈左衛大將軍、幽州都督、邢國公，賜東園秘器，陪葬昭陵。
value.en: Emperor Taizong deeply mourned him, posthumously appointing him Grand General of the Left Guard, Military Governor of Youzhou, and Duke of Xing State, granting him the Eastern Garden funerary vessels and permitting burial at Zhaoling.
value.literal: Emperor Taizong deeply mourned him, posthumously appointing him Grand General of the Left Guard, Military Governor of Youzhou, and Duke of Xing State, granting him the Eastern Garden funerary vessels and permitting burial at Zhaoling.

value.zh: 自春秋之後，禮義漸頹，風俗塵昏，愧恥心盡，疾走先得者爲上，奪攘投會者爲能。
value.en: After the Spring and Autumn period, ritual and righteousness gradually collapsed, custom grew dusty and dim, and the heart of shame was exhausted. Those who ran fastest and arrived first were esteemed; those who seized by force and seized opportunity were deemed capable.
value.literal: After the Spring and Autumn period, ritual and righteousness gradually collapsed, custom grew dusty and dim, and the heart of shame was exhausted. Those who ran fastest and arrived first were esteemed; those who seized by force and seized opportunity were deemed capable.

value.zh: 加以八世專齊，三家分晉，子貢之亂五國，蘇秦之鬥七雄，苛刻繁興，經籍道息，莫不長詐術，貴攻戰，萬姓皆戴爪牙，無人不屬觜距。
value.en: Moreover, the eight generations monopolized Qi, the three families divided Jin, Zigong threw five states into chaos, and Su Qin set seven powers at odds. Harshness and severity flourished, the way of the classics ceased, and all prized deceit and stratagem and value attack and warfare. The myriad people all wore claws and fangs; there was no one who did not possess beak and spur.
value.literal: Moreover, the eight generations monopolized Qi, the three families divided Jin, Zigong threw five states into chaos, and Su Qin set seven powers at odds. Harshness and severity flourished, the way of the classics ceased, and all prized deceit and stratagem and value attack and warfare. The myriad people all wore claws and fangs; there was no one who did not possess beak and spur.

value.zh: 所以商鞅欺故友，李斯囚舊交，孫臏喪足於龐涓，張儀得誌於陳軫。
value.en: Therefore Shang Yang deceived an old friend, Li Si imprisoned a former associate, Sun Bin lost his feet at the hands of Pang Juan, and Zhang Yi achieved his wish over Chen Zhen.
value.literal: Therefore Shang Yang deceived an old friend, Li Si imprisoned a former associate, Sun Bin lost his feet at the hands of Pang Juan, and Zhang Yi achieved his wish over Chen Zhen.

value.zh: 一旅之眾，便欲稱王；
value.en: A single company of men then wished to declare themselves kings;
value.literal: A single company of men then wished to declare themselves kings;

value.zh: 再戰之雄，爭來奉帝。
value.en: heroes who had fought twice contended to offer allegiance to an emperor.
value.literal: heroes who had fought twice contended to offer allegiance to an emperor.

value.zh: 先王會盟之禮，昔時樽俎之容，三代玄風，掃地至盡。
value.en: The alliance rites of former kings and the bearing of former times at the feast — the mysterious customs of the Three Dynasties were swept clean to the ground.
value.literal: The alliance rites of former kings and the bearing of former times at the feast — the mysterious customs of the Three Dynasties were swept clean to the ground.

value.zh: 況始皇削平區宇，殊非至公，李斯之作股肱，罕循大道，人無見德，唯虐是聞。
value.en: Moreover, when the First Emperor pacified the realm, it was by no means supremely fair. When Li Si served as his right arm, he rarely followed the great way. The people saw no virtue — they heard only cruelty.
value.literal: Moreover, when the First Emperor pacified the realm, it was by no means supremely fair. When Li Si served as his right arm, he rarely followed the great way. The people saw no virtue — they heard only cruelty.

value.zh: 當此時也，主猜於上，人駭於下，父不能保之於子，君不能得之於臣。
value.en: At that time the ruler was suspicious above and the people terrified below. Fathers could not preserve their sons; lords could not obtain their ministers.
value.literal: At that time the ruler was suspicious above and the people terrified below. Fathers could not preserve their sons; lords could not obtain their ministers.

value.zh: 欲使始皇分土奸雄，建侯薄俗，若喻晉、鄭之可依，便借賊兵而資盜糧，寄龍魚而助風雨，不可行也。
value.en: To wish to make the First Emperor divide territory among treacherous heroes and establish marquisates amid shallow custom — if one were to say that Jin and Zheng could be relied upon, it would be like lending weapons to bandits and supplying grain to robbers, entrusting dragons and fish and aiding wind and rain. It could not be done.
value.literal: To wish to make the First Emperor divide territory among treacherous heroes and establish marquisates amid shallow custom — if one were to say that Jin and Zheng could be relied upon, it would be like lending weapons to bandits and supplying grain to robbers, entrusting dragons and fish and aiding wind and rain. It could not be done.

value.zh: 是以秦鑒周德之綿深，懼己圖之不遠，罷侯置守，高下在心，天下製在一人，百姓不聞二主。
value.en: Therefore Qin took warning from Zhou's virtue extending deep and long, feared that its own design would not reach far, abolished marquisates and established governors. High and low were in its heart; the realm was controlled by one man, and the common people heard not of two masters.
value.literal: Therefore Qin took warning from Zhou's virtue extending deep and long, feared that its own design would not reach far, abolished marquisates and established governors. High and low were in its heart; the realm was controlled by one man, and the common people heard not of two masters.

value.zh: 直是不得行其世封，非薄功臣而賤骨肉也。
value.en: It was simply that hereditary enfeoffment could not be practiced — not that it slighted meritorious ministers or despised kin.
value.literal: It was simply that hereditary enfeoffment could not be practiced — not that it slighted meritorious ministers or despised kin.

value.zh: 桓彥範敬暉崔玄暐張柬之袁恕己
value.en: Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, Cui Xuanwei, Zhang Jianzhi, and Yuan Shuji
value.literal: Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, Cui Xuanwei, Zhang Jianzhi, Yuan Shuji

value.zh: 其年秋，柬之表請歸襄州養疾。
value.en: That autumn Jianzhi asked to return to Xiang Prefecture to recover from illness.
value.literal: That autumn Jianzhi memorialized requesting to return to Xiang Prefecture to nurse his illness.

value.zh: 許之，仍特授襄州刺史，又拜其子漪爲著作郎，令隨父之任。
value.en: The request was granted; he was specially appointed prefect of Xiang, and his son Yi was made drafting official and sent with him to his post.
value.literal: The request was granted; he was specially appointed prefect of Xiang Prefecture, and his son Yi was appointed drafting official and ordered to accompany his father to his post.

value.zh: 上親賦詩祖道，又令群公餞送於定鼎門外。
value.en: The emperor personally composed a farewell poem and had the assembled ministers see him off with a feast outside the Dingding Gate.
value.literal: The emperor personally composed a poem to send him off on the road, and also ordered the assembled lords to give a farewell feast outside the Dingding Gate.

value.zh: 柬之至襄州，有鄉親舊交抵罪者，必深文致法，無所縱舍。
value.en: Once in Xiang Prefecture, Jianzhi prosecuted kinsmen and old friends who had run afoul of the law with the utmost severity and showed no mercy.
value.literal: When Jianzhi reached Xiang Prefecture, if kinsmen or old acquaintances were charged with crimes, he always applied the law with the utmost severity and showed no leniency.

value.zh: 其子漪恃以立功，每見諸少長，不以禮接，時議以爲不能易荊楚之剽性焉。
value.en: His son Yi, relying on his father's standing, treated elders and juniors without proper courtesy; people said he could not change the fierce Jing-Chu temperament.
value.literal: His son Yi, relying on his father's achievements, whenever he met elders or juniors did not receive them with proper courtesy; contemporary opinion held that he could not change the fierce nature of Jing-Chu.

value.zh: 尋爲武三思所構，貶授新州司馬。
value.en: Soon Wu Sansi framed him, and he was demoted to military adjutant of Xin.
value.literal: Soon he was framed by Wu Sansi and demoted to military adjutant of Xin Prefecture.

value.zh: 柬之至新州，憤恚而卒，年八十餘，景雲元年，製曰：「褒德紀功，事華典冊；
value.en: Jianzhi reached Xin Prefecture, died in anger and resentment at over eighty, and in the first year of Jingyun an edict declared, "To honor virtue and record merit adorns the canonical records;
value.literal: When Jianzhi reached Xin Prefecture he died in anger and resentment, aged over eighty. In the first year of Jingyun an edict said, "To honor virtue and record merit is the splendor of canonical records;

value.zh: 飾終追遠，理光名教。
value.en: to adorn the end and recall the distant past illuminates the principles of moral teaching.
value.literal: to adorn the end and recall the distant past illuminates the principles of name and teaching.

value.zh: 故吏部尚書張柬之翼戴興運，謨明帝道，經綸謇諤，風範猶存。
value.en: The late Minister of Personnel Zhang Jianzhi aided the rising fortune, counseled with clarity on the imperial way, ordered the realm with forthright remonstrance, and his exemplary bearing still endures.
value.literal: The late Minister of Personnel Zhang Jianzhi aided and upheld the rising fortune, counseled with clarity on the imperial way, ordered the realm with forthright remonstrance, and his exemplary bearing still endures.

value.zh: 往屬回邪，構成釁咎，無辜放逐，淪沒荒遐。
value.en: Through perverse wickedness a cause of offense was fabricated; he was banished without guilt and lost in distant exile.
value.literal: Formerly, through perverse wickedness, a cause of offense was fabricated; he was banished without guilt and sank into distant exile.

value.zh: 言念勳賢，良深軫悼，宜加寵贈，式賁幽泉。
value.en: Remembering his merit, I am deeply grieved; he should receive added posthumous honors to adorn the realm below.
value.literal: Thinking on his meritorious worth, I am deeply grieved; he should receive added posthumous honors to adorn the hidden realm.

value.zh: 可贈中書令，封漢陽郡公。」
value.en: Let him be posthumously made Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Hanyang."
value.literal: He may be posthumously given the post of Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Hanyang commandery."

value.zh: 建中初，又贈司徒。
value.en: Early in Jianzhong he was again posthumously made Minister of Education.
value.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong he was again posthumously given the title Minister of Education.

value.zh: 崔光遠，滑州靈昌人也。
value.en: Cui Guangyuan came from Lingchang in Huazhou.
value.literal: Cui Guangyuan was a native of Lingchang in Huazhou.

value.zh: 本博陵舊族。
value.en: He was descended from the old Boling aristocracy.
value.literal: His clan was originally of the old Boling aristocracy.

value.zh: 祖敬嗣，好樗蒱飲酒。
value.en: His grandfather Jingsi was fond of gambling at chuck-a-luck and of wine.
value.literal: His grandfather Jingsi loved playing chuck-a-luck and drinking wine.

value.zh: 則天初，為房州刺史。
value.en: In the early years of Empress Wu, he served as prefect of Fangzhou.
value.literal: At the beginning of Empress Wu's reign, he served as prefect of Fang Prefecture.

value.zh: 中宗為廬陵王，安置在州，官吏多無禮度，敬嗣獨以親賢待之，供給豐贍，中宗深德之。
value.en: When Zhongzong was Prince of Luling and was kept at Fangzhou, most officials treated him without proper respect; only Jingsi received him as kin and as a man of worth and provided for him lavishly, and Zhongzong never forgot his kindness.
value.literal: When Zhongzong was Prince of Luling and was placed in that prefecture, most officials showed him no proper courtesy; Jingsi alone treated him with the affection due a kinsman and worthy, supplied him generously, and Zhongzong was deeply grateful.

value.zh: 及登位，有益州長史崔敬嗣，既同姓名，每進擬官，皆御筆超拜之者數四。
value.en: After Zhongzong took the throne, a chief administrator of Yizhou named Cui Jingsi shared the same name, and on four separate occasions when appointments were proposed the emperor personally marked him for extraordinary promotion.
value.literal: When Zhongzong ascended the throne, there was a Yizhou chief administrator named Cui Jingsi who bore the same name; whenever proposed appointments were submitted, the emperor four times used his own brush to promote him beyond the normal rank.

value.zh: 後引與語，始知誤寵。
value.en: Only when he later summoned the man to court did he discover his mistake.
value.literal: Later he summoned the man to speak with him and only then realized he had favored the wrong man.

value.zh: 訪敬嗣已卒，乃遣中書令韋安石授其子汪官。
value.en: On learning that Jingsi was dead, he sent Chief Minister Wei Anshi to grant an office to his son Wang.
value.literal: Learning that Jingsi had already died, he sent Chief Minister Wei Anshi to confer an office on his son Wang.

value.zh: 汪嗜酒不堪職任，且授洛州司功，又改五品。
value.en: Wang drank heavily and could not hold office, so he was first made Registrar of Luozhou and later demoted to fifth rank.
value.literal: Wang was addicted to wine and unfit for office; he was therefore given the post of Registrar of Luozhou, then reduced to fifth rank.

value.zh: 十五年六月，玄宗蒼黃幸蜀，大臣陳希烈、張倚等銜於失恩，不時赴難。
value.en: In the sixth month of year 15 Xuanzong fled in panic to Shu; ministers Chen Xilie and Zhang Yi, bitter over lost favor, did not hurry to his side.
value.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year Xuanzong fled in haste to Shu; grandees Chen Xilie and Zhang Yi and others, resentful at lost favor, did not hurry to the crisis.

value.zh: 琯結張均、張垍兄弟與韋述等行至城南十數里山寺，均、垍同行，皆以家在城中，逗留不進，琯獨馳蜀路。
value.en: Guan joined Zhang Jun and Zhang Ya with Wei Shu and reached a mountain temple south of the city; the Zhang brothers, with kin in the capital, hung back, while Guan alone raced toward Shu.
value.literal: Guan joined Zhang Jun and Zhang Ya and brothers with Wei Shu and others and went to a mountain temple ten-odd li south of the city; Jun and Ya, whose families were in the city, lingered and would not advance, but Guan alone galloped along the road to Shu.

value.zh: 七月，至普安郡謁見，玄宗大悅，即日拜文部尚書、同中書門下平章事，賜紫金魚袋。
value.en: In the seventh month he presented himself at Pu'an; Xuanzong was delighted and that day made him Minister of Culture, Grand Councillor, and gave him the gold-and-purple fish bag.
value.literal: In the seventh month he presented himself at Pu'an Commandery; Xuanzong was greatly pleased and that same day appointed him Minister of Culture, Grand Councillor with the Secretariat, and granted the gold and purple fish bag.

value.zh: 從幸成都，加銀青光祿大夫，仍與一子官。
value.en: He followed the court to Chengdu, received Silver and Blue Glory Grandee rank, and an office for one son.
value.literal: Following the court to Chengdu, he was given the silver and blue glory grandee rank and an office for one son.

value.zh: 其年八月，與左相韋見素、門下侍郎崔渙等奉使靈武，冊立肅宗。
value.en: That eighth month, with Left Chancellor Wei Jiansu and Vice Director Cui Huan, he went to Lingwu to invest Suzong.
value.literal: That eighth month, with Left Chancellor Wei Jiansu and Vice Director of the Secretariat Cui Huan and others, he was sent as envoy to Lingwu to invest Suzong.

value.zh: 至順化郡謁見，陳上皇傳付之旨，因言時事，詞情慷慨，肅宗為之改容。
value.en: At Shunhua he delivered the retired emperor's charge and spoke on affairs of the day with passion, and Suzong's face changed.
value.literal: Presenting himself at Shunhua Commandery, he declared the retired emperor's transmitted charge and spoke on current affairs with passionate words; Suzong's expression changed.

value.zh: 時潼關敗將王思禮、呂崇賁、李承光等引於纛下，將斬之，琯從容救諫，獨斬承光而已。
value.en: Defeated Tong Pass generals Wang Sili, Lü Chongben, and Li Chengguang were brought to the standards for execution; Guan calmly argued them down, and only Chengguang was killed.
value.literal: At that time the defeated generals from Tong Pass—Wang Sili, Lü Chongben, Li Chengguang, and others—were brought before the banners to be executed; Guan calmly remonstrated and only Chengguang was beheaded.

value.zh: 肅宗以琯素有重名，傾意待之，琯亦自負其才，以天下為己任。
value.en: Suzong, knowing Guan's long-standing fame, favored him wholeheartedly; Guan in turn trusted his own gifts and took the realm as his responsibility.
value.literal: Suzong, because Guan had long enjoyed a great reputation, treated him with full favor; Guan too relied on his talent and took the empire as his charge.

value.zh: 時行在機務，多決之於琯，凡有大事，諸將無敢預言。
value.en: At the mobile court most affairs were settled by Guan; on major matters the generals hardly dared speak.
value.literal: At the mobile court most business was decided by Guan; on great matters the generals did not dare speak.

value.zh: 尋抗疏自請將兵以誅寇孽，收復京都，肅宗望其成功，許之。
value.en: He soon asked in a memorial to lead troops against the rebels and recover the capital; Suzong hoped he would succeed and agreed.
value.literal: Soon he memorialized asking to lead troops to destroy the rebels and recover the capital; Suzong hoped for success and assented.

value.zh: 詔加持節、招討西京兼防禦蒲潼兩關兵馬節度等使，乃與子儀、光弼等計會進兵。
value.en: He was given full powers to reconnoiter the western capital and command the Pu and Tong garrisons, and planned advances with Ziyi and Guangbi.
value.literal: An edict added full powers as commissioner to reconnoiter the western capital and defend the armies of Pu and Tong passes, and he consulted with Ziyi, Guangbi, and others on advancing.

value.zh: 琯請自選參佐，乃以禦中史中丞鄧景山為副，戶部侍郎李揖為行軍司馬，中丞宋若思、起居郎知制誥賈至、右司郎中魏少遊為判官，給事中劉秩為參謀。
value.en: Guan chose his staff: Vice Censor-in-Chief Deng Jingshan as deputy, Vice Minister Li Yi as army marshal, Song Ruosi, Jia Zhi, and Wei Shaoyou as judges, and Liu Zhi as adviser.
value.literal: Guan asked to choose his own staff: Vice Censor-in-Chief Deng Jingshan as deputy, Vice Minister of Revenue Li Yi as army marshal, censors Song Ruosi and Jia Zhi and Right Department Director Wei Shaoyou as judges, and supervising secretary Liu Zhi as staff adviser.

value.zh: 既行，又令兵部尚書王思禮副之。
value.en: After he marched, Minister of War Wang Sili was added as deputy.
value.literal: After setting out, Minister of War Wang Sili was also made his deputy.

value.zh: 琯分為三軍：遣楊希文將南軍，自宜壽入；
value.en: Guan divided his force: Yang Xiwen would lead the southern army in from Yishou;
value.literal: Guan divided into three armies: Yang Xiwen was to lead the southern army in from Yishou;

value.zh: 劉悊將中軍，自武功入；
value.en: Liu Ti the central army from Wugong;
value.literal: Liu Ti was to lead the central army in from Wugong;

value.zh: 李光進將北軍，自奉天入。
value.en: Li Guangjin the northern army from Fengtian.
value.literal: Li Guangjin was to lead the northern army in from Fengtian.

value.zh: 琯自將中軍，為前鋒。
value.en: Guan himself commanded the central army as vanguard.
value.literal: Guan himself led the central army as vanguard.

value.zh: 十月庚子，師次便橋。
value.en: On gengzi in the tenth month the army camped at Bian Bridge.
value.literal: On the gengzi day of the tenth month the army halted at Bian Bridge.

value.zh: 辛丑，二軍先遇賊於咸陽縣之陳濤斜，接戰，官軍敗績。
value.en: On xinchou two armies met the rebels at Chentaoxie in Xianyang and were routed.
value.literal: On xinchou the two armies first met the rebels at Chentaoxie in Xianyang County; they joined battle and the government troops were defeated.

value.zh: 時琯用春秋車戰之法，以車二千乘，馬步夾之。
value.en: Guan fought by Spring and Autumn chariot rules, with two thousand chariots flanked by infantry and cavalry.
value.literal: At that time Guan used Spring and Autumn chariot warfare, with two thousand chariots and horse and foot on either side.

value.zh: 既戰，賊順風揚塵鼓噪，牛皆震駭，因縛芻縱火焚之，人畜撓敗，為所傷殺者四萬余人，存者數千而已。
value.en: In battle the rebels, wind at their backs, raised dust and clamor; oxen panicked, fodder was fired, men and beasts broke, more than forty thousand were killed or hurt, and only thousands remained.
value.literal: Once battle was joined the rebels, with the wind at their backs, raised dust and shouted; the oxen were terrified, fodder was bound and set afire, men and beasts were thrown into chaos, more than forty thousand were killed or wounded, and only a few thousand survived.

value.zh: 癸卯，琯又率南軍即戰，復敗，希文、劉悊並降於賊。
value.en: On guimao Guan led the southern army again, lost again, and Xiwen and Liu Ti surrendered.
value.literal: On guimao Guan again led the southern army into battle, was again defeated, and Xiwen and Liu Ti both surrendered to the rebels.

value.zh: 琯等奔赴行在，肉袒請罪，上並宥之。
value.en: Guan and his party rushed to the mobile court, stripped to the waist to beg punishment, and were all pardoned.
value.literal: Guan and the others ran to the mobile court, bared their torsos to ask punishment, and the emperor pardoned them all.

value.zh: 郭子儀子曜晞曖曙晤映晞子鋼曖子釗鏦釗子仲文族弟幼明子昕
value.en: Guo Ziyi's line included his sons Yao, Xi, Ai, Shu, Wu, and Ying, another son Xi, his son Gang, Ai's son Zhao (whose sons were Cong and Zhongwen), and his clansman Youming's son Xin.
value.literal: Guo Ziyi's sons: Yao, Xi, Ai, Shu, Wu, Ying, and Xi; Ziyi's son Gang; Ai's son Zhao; Zhao's sons Cong and Zhongwen; clan younger brother Youming's son Xin.

value.zh: 曜，子儀長子。
value.en: Yao was Ziyi's eldest son.
value.literal: Yao was Ziyi's eldest son.

value.zh: 性孝友廉謹。
value.en: He was filial, friendly, honest, and careful.
value.literal: By nature filial, friendly, honest, and careful.

value.zh: 子儀薨，出征於外，留曜治家，少長千人，皆得其所。
value.en: When Ziyi died on campaign, Yao ran the household of a thousand kin fairly.
value.literal: When Ziyi died, campaigning abroad, he left Yao to manage the house; old and young a thousand—all obtained their place.

value.zh: 諸弟爭飾池館，盛其車服，曜以儉樸自處。
value.en: Brothers flaunted wealth; Yao lived plainly.
value.literal: Younger brothers competed to adorn pools and halls and magnify carriage and dress; Yao kept himself frugal and plain.

value.zh: 累遷至太子賓客。
value.en: He rose to crown prince's guest.
value.literal: He successively rose to Crown Prince's Guest.

value.zh: 建中初，子儀罷兵柄，乃遍加諸子官，以曜為太子少保。
value.en: When Ziyi lost command, Yao became crown prince's junior mentor.
value.literal: At the start of Jianzhong, when Ziyi lost military power, he broadly added offices to the sons, making Yao Crown Prince's Junior Mentor.

value.zh: 子儀曜遵遺命，四朝所賜名馬珍玩，悉皆上獻，德宗復賜之，曜乃散諸昆弟。
value.en: They surrendered imperial gifts per Ziyi's will; Dezong returned them and Yao shared them among kin.
value.literal: Ziyi and Yao followed the testament: famous horses and precious playthings granted by the four reigns were all presented above; Dezong returned them, and Yao then distributed them among the brothers.

value.zh: 子儀薨後，楊炎、盧杞相次秉政，奸諂用事，尤忌勛族。
value.en: After Ziyi's death Yang Yan and Lu Qi persecuted great clans.
value.literal: After Ziyi's death, Yang Yan and Lu Qi successively held power; wicked flatterers handled affairs, especially jealous of meritorious clans.

value.zh: 子儀之婿太仆卿趙縱、少府少監李洞清、光祿卿王宰，皆以有人告訐細過，相次貶黜。
value.en: Sons-in-law Zhao Zong, Li Dongqing, and Wang Zai were demoted on petty denunciations.
value.literal: Ziyi's sons-in-law Grand Master of the Imperial Stud Zhao Zong, Vice Director of the Palace Workshops Li Dongqing, and Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Wang Zai—all because someone informed on minor faults were in succession demoted and dismissed.

value.zh: 曜家大恐，賴宰相張鎰力為庇護。
value.en: Yao's family feared ruin until Zhang Yi protected them.
value.literal: Yao's household was greatly afraid, relying on chief councilor Zhang Yi to exert strength in shelter.

value.zh: 奸人幸其危懼，多論奪田宅奴婢，曜不敢訴。
value.en: Predators seized their property while Yao dared not protest.
value.literal: Wicked men, rejoicing in their peril and fear, mostly argued to seize fields, houses, and slaves; Yao did not dare complain.

value.zh: 德宗微知之，詔曰：「尚父子儀，有大勛力，保乂皇家，嘗誓以山河，琢之金石，十世之宥，其可忘也！
value.en: Dezong decreed: "Imperial Father Ziyi's ten-generation pardon must not be forgotten!
value.literal: Dezong slightly knew this and issued an edict: "Imperial Father Guo Ziyi had great merit and strength, preserving and comforting the royal house; he once swore on mountains and rivers, carved on metal and stone—a pardon for ten generations—how can it be forgotten!

value.zh: 其家前時與人為市，以子儀身歿，名被誣構，欲論奪之，有司無得為理。」
value.en: If in former times his family made purchases from others, and now, because Ziyi himself has died and his name is falsely entangled, someone wishes to contest and seize them, the responsible offices must not process the claim."
value.literal: If in former times his family made purchases from others, and now, because Ziyi himself has died and his name is falsely entangled, someone wishes to contest and seize them, the responsible offices must not process the claim."

value.zh: 詔下方已。
value.en: When the edict was promulgated, the seizures stopped.
value.literal: When the edict was issued below, it stopped.

value.zh: 曜居喪得禮，若儒家子，服未闋寢疾，或勸其茹蔥薤，曜竟不屬口。
value.en: Yao mourned by Confucian rites; ill before mourning ended, he refused even scallions and leeks.
value.literal: Yao observed mourning with proper rites like a Confucian son; before mourning ended he took to bed with illness; some urged him to eat scallions and leeks; Yao ultimately did not put them to mouth.

value.zh: 建中四年三月卒，贈太子太傅。
value.en: In Jianzhong 4, third month, he died and was posthumously made grand mentor of the crown prince.
value.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Jianzhong he died; posthumously granted Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.

value.zh: 潘孟陽，禮部侍郎炎之子也。
value.en: Pan Mengyang was the son of Yan, Minister of Rites.
value.literal: Pan Mengyang was the son of Yan, Vice Minister of Rites.

value.zh: 孟陽以父廕進，登博學宏辭科。
value.en: Mengyang entered service through his father's privilege and passed the Boxue Hongci examination.
value.literal: Mengyang advanced through his father's yin privilege and passed the Broad Learning and Eloquent Expression examination.

value.zh: 累遷殿中侍御史，降為司議郎。
value.en: He rose to Palace Censor, then was demoted to Secretariat Drafter.
value.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Palace Censor, then demoted to Secretariat Drafter.

value.zh: 孟陽母，劉晏女也。
value.en: Mengyang's mother was Liu Yan's daughter.
value.literal: Mengyang's mother was a daughter of Liu Yan.

value.zh: 公卿多父友及外祖賓從，故得薦用，累至兵部郎中。
value.en: Many high officials were friends of his father or associates of his maternal grandfather, so he won recommendations and rose to bureau director in the Ministry of War.
value.literal: Many ministers and officials were his father's friends and his maternal grandfather's associates and followers, so he was recommended for appointment and rose to Bureau Director of the Ministry of War.

value.zh: 裴度領太原，署為參謀。
value.en: When Pei Du governed Taiyuan he appointed Rong staff planner.
value.literal: When Pei Du governed Taiyuan he appointed him as staff planner.

value.zh: 時王承宗據鎮州叛，度請戎單車往諭之，承宗感泣受教。
value.en: When Wang Chengzong held Zhen Prefecture in rebellion, Du asked Rong to go alone to instruct him, and Chengzong wept and accepted instruction.
value.literal: At the time Wang Chengzong held Zhen Prefecture in rebellion; Du asked Rong to go alone in a single carriage to instruct him, and Chengzong wept and accepted instruction.

value.zh: 入為殿中侍御史，累拜吏部郎中，遷諫議大夫。
value.en: He entered court as palace censor, rose to bureau director of personnel, and became censor.
value.literal: He entered court as Palace Censor and was repeatedly promoted to Bureau Director of the Ministry of Personnel and then Censor.

value.zh: 尋為劍南東、西兩川宣慰使。
value.en: He was soon made pacification commissioner of Eastern and Western Sichuan.
value.literal: He was soon made pacification commissioner of the Eastern and Western Sichuan circuits.

value.zh: 西州承蠻寇之後，戎既宣撫，兼再定征稅，廢置得所，公私便之。
value.en: Western prefectures, having suffered barbarian raids, were pacified by Rong; levies were reassessed, abolitions and establishments were appropriate, and public and private alike benefited.
value.literal: The western prefectures, having suffered barbarian raids, were both pacified by Rong and had their levies reassessed; abolitions and establishments were appropriate, and public and private alike benefited.

value.zh: 還，拜給事中，駁奏為當時所稱。
value.en: On return he became drafting attendant; his memorials of rejection were praised at the time.
value.literal: On his return he was appointed Drafting Attendant; his memorials of rejection were praised at the time.

value.zh: 改華州刺史，遷兗海沂密都團練觀察等使。
value.en: He became governor of Hua and overall training and surveillance commissioner of Yan, Hai, Yi, and Mi.
value.literal: He was changed to governor of Hua Prefecture and transferred to overall training and surveillance commissioner of Yan, Hai, Yi, and Mi.

value.zh: 將行，州人戀惜遮道，至有解靴斷登者。
value.en: As he was about to depart, reluctant people blocked the road; some even pulled off boots and broke carriage steps.
value.literal: As he was about to depart, the people, reluctant to part with him, blocked the road; some even pulled off boots and broke carriage steps.

value.zh: 理兗一年，大和八年五月卒，贈禮部尚書。
value.en: After governing Yan one year he died in the fifth month of Dahe 8 and was posthumously made minister of rites.
value.literal: After governing Yan for one year he died in the fifth month of the eighth year of Dahe and was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.

value.zh: 毅夫，登進士第。
value.en: Yifu passed the jinshi examination.
value.literal: Yifu passed the jinshi examination.

value.zh: 初正甫兄式，大歷中進士登第，繼之以正甫，式子元夫、傑夫、征夫又相次登科。
value.en: At first Zhengfu's elder brother Shi passed the jinshi in the Dalu era, followed by Zhengfu; Shi's sons Yuanfu, Jiefu, and Zhengfu passed in succession.
value.literal: At first Zhengfu's elder brother Shi passed the jinshi in the Dalu era, followed by Zhengfu; Shi's sons Yuanfu, Jiefu, and Zhengfu in turn passed the examination in succession.

value.zh: 太和中，文章之盛，世共稱之。
value.en: In the Taihe era the flourishing of literary talent was praised by the age.
value.literal: In the Taihe era the flourishing of literary talent was praised together by the age.

value.zh: 元夫，太和初兵部郎中、知制誥，遷中書舍人，出為汝州刺史。
value.en: Yuanfu, early in Taihe, was war bureau director and drafting drafter, rose to drafting attendant, and was sent out as governor of Ru.
value.literal: Yuanfu, early in Taihe, was Bureau Director of the Ministry of War and drafting drafter, was promoted to Drafting Attendant, and was sent out as governor of Ru Prefecture.

value.zh: 毅夫位至戶部侍郎、弘文館學士判院事。
value.en: Yifu rose to vice minister of revenue and Hongwen Hall academician with charge of the academy.
value.literal: Yifu rose to Vice Minister of Revenue and academician of the Hongwen Hall with charge of the academy.

value.zh: 諸群從登第者數人，而毅夫子祎最知名。
value.en: Several cousins passed the examination; among them Yifu's son Yi was most renowned.
value.literal: Several cousins passed the examination; among them Yifu's son Yi was most renowned.

value.zh: 朱泚黃巢秦宗權
value.en: Zhu Ci, Huang Chao, and Qin Zongquan.
value.literal: Zhu Ci, Huang Chao, and Qin Zongquan.

value.zh: 德宗嗣位，加太子太師、鳳翔尹，實封至三百戶。
value.en: When Dezong succeeded to the throne, Zhu Ci was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and prefect of Fengxiang, and his substantive fief was increased to three hundred households.
value.literal: When Dezong succeeded to the throne, Ci was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and prefect of Fengxiang, and his substantive fief was raised to three hundred households.

value.zh: 建中元年，涇州將劉文喜阻兵為亂，加泚四鎮北庭行軍、涇原節度使，與諸軍討之。
value.en: In the first year of Jianzhong, Jingzhou general Liu Wenxi mutinied and rebelled. Zhu Ci was made commander of the Four Garrisons and Beiting campaign and military commissioner of Jingyuan, and led the allied armies against him.
value.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong, Jingzhou general Liu Wenxi blocked the army and made rebellion; Ci was made commander of the Four Garrisons and Beiting campaign and military commissioner of Jingyuan, and with the various armies punished him.

value.zh: 涇州平，加泚中書令，還鎮鳳翔，而以舒王讓遙領涇原節度。
value.en: After Jingzhou was pacified, Zhu Ci was made Grand Secretariat Director and returned to garrison Fengxiang, while Prince Shu Li Rang was given nominal command of Jingyuan.
value.literal: When Jingzhou was pacified, Ci was made Grand Secretariat Director, returned to garrison Fengxiang, and Prince Shu Li Rang was made titular military commissioner of Jingyuan.

value.zh: 二年，加泚太尉。
value.en: In the second year Zhu Ci was made Grand Preceptor.
value.literal: In the second year Ci was made Grand Preceptor.

value.zh: 朱滔將反叛，陰使人與泚計議，以帛書納蠟丸中，置髮髻間。
value.en: Zhu Tao was plotting rebellion and secretly sent a messenger to consult with Zhu Ci, concealing a silk letter inside a wax pellet hidden in the messenger's hair bun.
value.literal: Zhu Tao was about to rebel; secretly he sent a man to consult with Ci, placing a silk letter inside a wax pellet and hiding it in his hair bun.

value.zh: 河東節度馬燧搜獲之，以聞，並送帛書及所遣使。
value.en: Hedong military commissioner Ma Sui seized the messenger, reported to the throne, and forwarded both the silk letter and the envoy.
value.literal: Hedong military commissioner Ma Sui searched and seized it, reported to the throne, and sent up both the silk letter and the envoy dispatched.

value.zh: 泚惶懼，頓首乞歸罪有司。
value.en: Zhu Ci was terrified and prostrated himself, begging to surrender himself to the authorities for judgment.
value.literal: Ci was fearful and in panic, bowing his head and begging to surrender himself to the authorities for punishment.

value.zh: 上勉之曰：「千里不同謀，非卿之過。」
value.en: The emperor reassured him: "You were a thousand li apart and did not plot together—this is not your fault."
value.literal: The emperor comforted him, saying: "A thousand li apart, you did not plot together—this is not your fault."

value.zh: 三年四月，以張鎰代泚為鳳翔隴右節度留後，留泚京師，加實封至一千戶，與一子正員官，其幽州盧龍節度、太尉、中書令並如故。
value.en: In the fourth month of the third year Zhang Yi replaced Zhu Ci as acting military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou. Zhu Ci was kept at the capital, his substantive fief was raised to one thousand households, and one of his sons was given a regular official post; his titles as military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Secretariat Director remained unchanged.
value.literal: In the fourth month of the third year Zhang Yi replaced Ci as acting military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou; Ci was kept at the capital, his substantive fief was raised to one thousand households, and one son was given a regular official post; his posts as military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Secretariat Director remained as before.

value.zh: 本紀第一 太祖一
value.en: Annals 1: Taizu, Part One
value.literal: Annals 1, Taizu 1

value.zh: 二十年春二月，元福建行省參政袁天祿以福寧降。
value.en: In the second month of spring in the twentieth year Yuan Tianlu, associate administrator of the Fujian Branch Secretariat, surrendered Funing.
value.literal: In the second month of spring in the twentieth year Yuan Fujian Branch Secretariat Associate Administrator Yuan Tianlu submitted Funing.

value.zh: 三月戊子，征劉基、宋濂、章溢、葉琛至。
value.en: On wuzi day in the third month he summoned Liu Ji, Song Lian, Zhang Yi, and Ye Chen to court.
value.literal: On the day wuzi of the third month he summoned Liu Ji, Song Lian, Zhang Yi, and Ye Chen to come.

value.zh: 夏五月，徐達、常遇春敗陳友諒於池州。
value.en: In the fifth month of summer Xu Da and Chang Yuchun defeated Chen Youliang at Chizhou.
value.literal: In the fifth month of summer Xu Da and Chang Yuchun defeated Chen Youliang at Chizhou.

value.zh: 閏月丙辰，友諒陷太平，守將朱文遜，院判花雲、王鼎，知府許瑗死之。
value.en: On bingchen day in the intercalary month Youliang seized Taiping; the defender Zhu Wensun, Vice Commissioners Hua Yun and Wang Ding, and Prefect Xu Yuan were killed.
value.literal: In the intercalary month, day bingchen, Youliang took Taiping; the defending general Zhu Wensun, administrative vice commissioner Hua Yun and Wang Ding, and prefect Xu Yuan died for it.

value.zh: 未幾，友諒弒其主徐壽輝，自稱皇帝，國號漢，盡有江西、湖廣地，約士誠合攻應天，應天大震。
value.en: Soon after, Youliang murdered his master Xu Shouhui, declared himself emperor of Han, held all Jiangxi and Huguang, and joined Zhang Shicheng in a planned assault on Yingtian—the capital was thrown into alarm.
value.literal: Before long Youliang murdered his lord Xu Shouhui, styled himself emperor, state title Han, fully held Jiangxi and Huguang lands, and agreed with Shicheng to jointly attack Yingtian—Yingtian was greatly shaken.

value.zh: 諸將議先復太平以牽之，太祖曰：「不可。
value.en: His commanders urged recapturing Taiping first to pin Youliang down; Taizu said, "No.
value.literal: The generals discussed first recovering Taiping to pin him; Taizu said: "Cannot.

value.zh: 彼居上游，舟師十倍於我，猝難復也。」
value.en: He holds the upper river; his fleet outnumbers ours ten to one—we cannot retake Taiping in a rush."
value.literal: He occupies the upper reaches; his naval forces are ten times ours—suddenly hard to recover."

value.zh: 或請自將迎擊，太祖曰：「不可。
value.en: Some urged him to lead the army out to meet them; Taizu said, "No.
value.literal: Some asked him to lead in person to meet the attack; Taizu said: "Cannot.

value.zh: 彼以偏師綴我，而全軍趨金陵，順流半日可達，吾步騎急難引還，百里趨戰，兵法所忌，非策也。」
value.en: He would tie us down with a diversion while his main fleet raced for Jinling—half a day's sail downstream. Our foot and horse could not turn back in time; to fight a hundred li from home is what doctrine forbids."
value.literal: He would use a detached force to detain us while his full army rushed Jinling—downstream half a day could reach; our infantry and cavalry urgently hard to pull back—a hundred li to rush to battle is what military law forbids; not a strategy."

value.zh: 乃馳諭胡大海搗信州牽其後，而令康茂才以書紿友諒，令速來。
value.en: He galloped orders to Hu Dahai to raid Xinzhou and threaten Youliang's rear, and had Kang Maocai lure him east with a forged letter.
value.literal: He then galloped orders to Hu Dahai to strike Xinzhou in the rear to pull him, and ordered Kang Maocai with a letter to deceive Youliang and make him come quickly.

value.zh: 友諒果引兵東。
value.en: Youliang took the bait and marched east.
value.literal: Youliang indeed led troops east.

value.zh: 於是常遇春伏石灰山，徐達陣南門外，楊璟屯大勝港，張德勝等以舟師出龍江關，太祖親督軍盧龍山。
value.en: Chang Yuchun hid at Lime Mountain, Xu Da formed line at the south gate, Yang Jing held Dasheng Harbor, Zhang Desheng and others took the fleet out through Longjiang Pass, and Taizu commanded in person from Lulong Mountain.
value.literal: Thereupon Chang Yuchun lay in ambush at Lime Mountain, Xu Da formed battle at the south gate, Yang Jing encamped at Dasheng Harbor, Zhang Desheng and others with naval forces issued from Longjiang Pass, and Taizu personally supervised the army at Lulong Mountain.

value.zh: 乙丑，友諒至龍灣，眾欲戰，太祖曰：「天且雨，趣食，乘雨擊之。」
value.en: On yichou day Youliang reached Longwan; his men wanted to fight at once; Taizu said, "Rain is coming—eat first, then strike in the storm."
value.literal: On the day yichou Youliang reached Longwan; the crowd wished to fight; Taizu said: "Heaven will soon rain—hurry and eat, strike them in the rain."

value.zh: 須臾，果大雨，士卒競奮，雨止合戰，水陸夾擊，大破之，友諒乘別舸走。
value.en: Rain burst upon them; the troops fought all the harder; when it cleared they closed on land and water together, shattered the Han fleet, and Youliang fled in a small boat.
value.literal: In a moment rain indeed fell heavily; soldiers competed in vigor; when rain stopped they joined battle; land and water attacked from both sides and greatly defeated them; Youliang rode another boat and fled.

value.zh: 遂復太平，下安慶，而大海亦克信州。
value.en: He recovered Taiping, took Anqing, and Hu Dahai seized Xinzhou as well.
value.literal: He then recovered Taiping, took Anqing, and Dahai also took Xinzhou.

value.zh: 初，太祖令茂才紿友諒，李善長以為疑。
value.en: Earlier Taizu had ordered Maocai's ruse; Li Shanchang had doubted it.
value.literal: Earlier Taizu had ordered Maocai to deceive Youliang; Li Shanchang thought it doubtful.

value.zh: 太祖曰：「二寇合，吾首尾受敵，惟速其來而先破之，則士誠膽落矣。」
value.en: Taizu said, "With both enemies allied we would be caught between them—only by drawing Youliang in and breaking him first will Shicheng lose heart."
value.literal: Taizu said: "The two bandits united—we receive the enemy front and rear; only by hastening his coming and first breaking him will Shicheng's courage fall."

value.zh: 已而士誠兵竟不出。
value.en: In the end Zhang Shicheng's troops never marched.
value.literal: Before long Shicheng's troops indeed did not come out.

value.zh: 丁卯，置儒學提舉司，以宋濂為提舉，遣子標受經學。
value.en: On dingmao day he established the Confucian Learning Promotion Office under Song Lian and set his son Biao to the classics.
value.literal: On the day dingmao he established the Confucian Learning Promotion Office, with Song Lian as promoter, and sent his son Biao to receive classical learning.

value.zh: 六月，耿再成敗石抹宜孫於慶元，宜孫戰死，遣使祭之。
value.en: In the sixth month Geng Zaocheng defeated Shimo Yisun at Qingyuan; Yisun fell in battle and Taizu sent envoys to sacrifice to him.
value.literal: In the sixth month Geng Zaocheng defeated Shimo Yisun at Qingyuan; Yisun died in battle; he sent envoys to offer sacrifice.

value.zh: 秋九月，徐壽輝舊將歐普祥以袁州降。
value.en: In the ninth month of autumn Ou Pu Xiang, a former officer of Xu Shouhui, surrendered Yuanzhou.
value.literal: In the ninth month of autumn Xu Shouhui's old general Ou Pu Xiang submitted Yuanzhou.

value.zh: 冬十二月，復遣夏煜以書諭國珍。
value.en: In the twelfth month of winter he again sent Xia Yu with a letter summoning Guozhen.
value.literal: In the twelfth month of winter he again sent Xia Yu with a letter to instruct Guozhen.

value.zh: 硃亮祖
value.en: Zhu Liangzu
value.literal: Zhu Liangzu

value.zh: 二十六年二月，錦衣衛指揮蔣瓛告玉謀反，下吏鞫訊。
value.en: In the second month of the twenty-sixth year the brocade-coated guard commander Jiang Huan reported that Yu was plotting rebellion. Yu was handed over for interrogation.
value.literal: In the second month of the twenty-sixth year the Brocade-Coated Guard Commander Jiang Huan reported that Yu plotted rebellion; he was handed to officials for interrogation.

value.zh: 獄辭云：「玉同景川侯曹震、鶴慶侯張翼、舳艫侯硃壽、東莞伯何榮及吏部尚書詹徽、戶部侍郎傅友文等謀為變，將伺帝出耤田舉事。」
value.en: The confession stated that Yu, together with the Marquis of Jingchuan Cao Zhen, the Marquis of Heqing Zhang Yi, the Marquis of Scullion Zhu Shou, the Earl of Dongguan He Rong, the minister of personnel Zhan Hui, the vice minister of revenue Fu Youwen, and others, plotted a revolt and intended to strike when the emperor went out for the plowing ceremony."
value.literal: The prison confession stated, "Yu together with the Marquis of Jingchuan Cao Zhen, the Marquis of Heqing Zhang Yi, the Marquis of Scullion Zhu Shou, the Earl of Dongguan He Rong, and the Ministers of Personnel Zhan Hui and Revenue Fu Youwen and others plotted a revolt, intending to wait until the emperor went out to the plowing ceremony to raise the affair."

value.zh: 獄具，族誅之。
value.en: When the case was complete, Yu and his associates were executed to the third degree.
value.literal: When the case was complete, the clans were exterminated.

value.zh: 列侯以下坐黨夷滅者不可勝數。
value.en: The marquises and lesser nobles punished by association were beyond counting.
value.literal: Marquises and below who were punished by association and exterminated were beyond counting.

value.zh: 手詔佈告天下，條列爰書為《逆臣錄》。
value.en: The emperor issued a hand-edict to the realm, publishing the written confession as the Record of Rebellious Ministers.
value.literal: A hand-edict was promulgated throughout the realm, itemizing the written confession as the Record of Rebellious Ministers.

value.zh: 至九月，乃下詔曰：「藍賊為亂，謀泄，族誅者萬五千人。
value.en: In the ninth month an edict was issued: "The traitor Lan raised a rebellion. When the plot was exposed, fifteen thousand people were executed by association.
value.literal: By the ninth month an edict was then issued, saying, "The bandit Lan raised disorder; when the plot was exposed, those exterminated by clan numbered fifteen thousand.

value.zh: 自今胡黨、藍黨概赦不問。」
value.en: Henceforth members of the Hu and Lan factions are altogether pardoned and will not be pursued."
value.literal: From now on the Hu faction and the Lan faction are altogether pardoned and not to be pursued."

value.zh: 胡謂丞相惟庸也。
value.en: "Hu" refers to the chancellor Hu Weiyong.
value.literal: Hu refers to the Chancellor Hu Weiyong.

value.zh: 於是元功宿將相繼盡矣。
value.en: With this, the founding merit-holders and veteran generals were successively wiped out.
value.literal: Thus the founding merit-holders and veteran generals were in succession exhausted.

value.zh: 凡列名《逆臣錄》者，一公、十三侯、二伯。
value.en: Those named in the Record of Rebellious Ministers numbered one duke, thirteen marquises, and two earls.
value.literal: All those listed by name in the Record of Rebellious Ministers numbered one duke, thirteen marquises, and two earls.

value.zh: 葉升前坐事誅，胡玉等諸小侯皆別見。
