value.en: Ye Sheng had already been executed on other charges; the lesser marquises such as Hu Yu are recorded elsewhere.
value.literal: Ye Sheng had earlier been executed for another matter; the lesser marquises such as Hu Yu are recorded separately.

value.zh: 其曹震、張翼、張溫、陳桓、硃壽、曹興六侯，附著左方。
value.en: The six marquises Cao Zhen, Zhang Yi, Zhang Wen, Chen Huan, Zhu Shou, and Cao Xing are appended below.
value.literal: The six marquises Cao Zhen, Zhang Yi, Zhang Wen, Chen Huan, Zhu Shou, and Cao Xing are appended on the left.

value.zh: 陶安，字主敬，當塗人。
value.en: Tao An, styled Zhujing, was from Dangtu.
value.literal: Tao An, with the style name Zhujing, was a man of Dangtu.

value.zh: 少敏悟，博涉經史，尤長於《易》。
value.en: As a youth he was exceptionally quick-witted; he read widely in the classics and histories and was especially skilled in the Book of Changes.
value.literal: In youth he was perceptive and quick; he ranged broadly through the classics and histories, and was especially accomplished in the Book of Changes.

value.zh: 元至正初，舉江浙鄉試，授明道書院山長，避亂家居。
value.en: Early in the Zhizheng reign, he passed the Jiang and Zhe regional examination and was appointed director of the Mingdao Academy; he then retired at home to escape the civil unrest.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan Zhizheng era, he passed the Jiang-Zhe provincial examination, was appointed headmaster of the Mingdao Academy, and stayed at home to avoid the turmoil.

value.zh: 太祖取太平，安與耆儒李習率父老出迎。
value.en: When the founding emperor captured Taiping, An and the elder scholar Li Xi led the local elders out to welcome him.
value.literal: When the Taizu emperor took Taiping, An together with the venerable scholar Li Xi led the elders to go out and welcome him.

value.zh: 太祖召與語。
value.en: The emperor summoned him for an audience.
value.literal: The Taizu emperor summoned him and conversed with him.

value.zh: 安進曰：「海內鼎沸，豪傑並爭，然其意在子女玉帛，非有撥亂、救民、安天下心。
value.en: An spoke up: "The empire is in uproar and rival strongmen fight one another, but their aim is spoil and luxury, not to restore order, relieve the people, or bring peace to the realm.
value.literal: An advanced and said: "Within the seas the tripod boils; heroes struggle with one another, yet their intent lies in children, women, jade, and silks—they lack the mind to put chaos in order, save the people, and settle all under Heaven.

value.zh: 明公渡江，神武不殺，人心悅服，應天順人。
value.en: Your Grace has crossed the Yangzi with a martial spirit that shuns needless slaughter; the people gladly submit. You answer Heaven's mandate and win men over.
value.literal: My lord has crossed the Yangzi: divine in martial prowess and sparing in killing; hearts rejoice and submit—he responds to Heaven and accords with men.

value.zh: 以行吊伐，天下不足平也。」
value.en: March forth as the champion of the wronged, and pacifying the realm will be a small matter."
value.literal: By acting as one who comforts the wronged and punishes the guilty, all under Heaven is not enough to remain un pacified."

value.zh: 太祖問曰：「吾欲取金陵，何如？」
value.en: The emperor asked, "I mean to take Jinling. What do you think?"
value.literal: The Taizu emperor asked: "I wish to take Jinling—how would that be?"

value.zh: 安曰：「金陵，古帝王都。
value.en: An replied, "Jinling was the seat of emperors in antiquity.
value.literal: An said: "Jinling is the ancient capital of emperors and kings.

value.zh: 取而有之，撫形勝以臨四方，何向不克？」
value.en: Seize it and hold its strategic heights to command the four quarters—what enemy could withstand you?"
value.literal: Take it and possess it; soothe its commanding terrain to look down on the four directions—what direction would not be overcome?"

value.zh: 太祖曰：「善。」
value.en: The emperor said, "Well said."
value.literal: The Taizu emperor said: "Good."

value.zh: 留參幕府，授左司員外郎，以習為太平知府。
value.en: He was retained on the military staff as Left Department Assistant Director, and Li Xi was appointed prefect of Taiping.
value.literal: He was kept to participate in the staff headquarters and appointed Left Department Assistant Director; Li Xi was made Taiping prefect.

value.zh: 習字伯羽，年八十余矣，卒於官。
value.en: Li Xi, styled Boyu, was over eighty and died in his post.
value.literal: Xi, style name Boyu, was more than eighty years old and died in office.

value.zh: 安從克集慶，進郎中。
value.en: An accompanied the campaign that took Jiqing and was promoted to Director in the Secretariat.
value.literal: An followed in the conquest of Jiqing and was promoted to Director.

value.zh: 及聘劉基、宋濂、章溢、葉琛至，太祖問安：「四人者何如？」
value.en: When Liu Ji, Song Lian, Zhang Yi, and Ye Chen were brought in, the emperor asked An, "What do you make of these four?"
value.literal: When Liu Ji, Song Lian, Zhang Yi, and Ye Chen were invited and arrived, the Taizu emperor asked An: "How are these four men?"

value.zh: 對曰：「臣謀略不如基，學問不如濂，治民之才不如溢、琛。」
value.en: He answered, "Your servant is no match for Ji in strategy, for Lian in scholarship, or for Yi and Chen in governing the people."
value.literal: He replied: "In strategy and planning your subject is not equal to Ji; in learning not equal to Lian; in talent to govern the people not equal to Yi and Chen."

value.zh: 太祖多其能讓。
value.en: The emperor admired his modesty.
value.literal: The Taizu emperor greatly valued his ability to yield.

value.zh: 黃州初下，思得重臣鎮之，無逾安者，遂命知黃州。
value.en: When Huangzhou was newly pacified, the emperor sought a senior official to secure it and found no one better than An, so he appointed him Huangzhou magistrate.
value.literal: When Huangzhou was first taken, he thought to obtain a weighty minister to guard it; none surpassed An, so he was ordered to govern Huangzhou.

value.zh: 寬租省徭，民以樂業。
value.en: He reduced rents and levies, and the people settled contentedly into their work.
value.literal: He eased rents and reduced corvée labor; the people thereby took joy in their occupations.

value.zh: 坐事謫知桐城，移知饒州。
value.en: After a disciplinary offense he was demoted to Tongcheng and later transferred to Raozhou.
value.literal: For an offense he was demoted to govern Tongcheng, then transferred to govern Raozhou.

value.zh: 陳友定兵攻城，安召吏民諭以順逆，嬰城固守。
value.en: When Chen Youding's army besieged the city, An rallied officials and commoners, explained the difference between loyalty and rebellion, and held the walls in a stubborn defense.
value.literal: Chen Youding's troops attacked the city; An summoned officials and people and instructed them on obedience and rebellion; they closed the city and firmly defended.

value.zh: 援兵至，敗去。
value.en: When relief arrived, the besiegers were defeated and withdrew.
value.literal: Relief troops arrived and Chen's forces were defeated and withdrew.

value.zh: 諸將欲盡戮民之從寇者，安不可。
value.en: The generals wanted to execute every civilian who had sided with the enemy, but An refused.
value.literal: The various generals wished to slaughter all among the people who had followed the bandit; An would not permit it.

value.zh: 太祖賜詩褒美，州民建生祠事之。
value.en: The emperor granted him a poem of commendation, and the people of the prefecture raised a living shrine in his honor.
value.literal: The Taizu emperor bestowed a poem in praise; the people of the prefecture built a living shrine to serve him.

value.zh: 洪武元年，命知制誥兼修國史。
value.en: In the first Hongwu year he was charged with drafting edicts and compiling the dynastic history.
value.literal: In Hongwu year one he was ordered to draft imperial proclamations and concurrently edit the national history.

value.zh: 帝嘗御東閣，與安及章溢等論前代興亡本末。
value.en: The emperor once held court in the Eastern Lodge and debated with An, Zhang Yi, and others the causes of rise and fall in earlier dynasties.
value.literal: The emperor once took the eastern pavilion and with An and Zhang Yi and others discussed the roots and ends of the rise and fall of former ages.

value.zh: 安言喪亂之源，由於驕侈。
value.en: An argued that the root of dynastic collapse was arrogance and lavish excess.
value.literal: An said the source of ruin and disorder lies in arrogance and extravagance.

value.zh: 帝曰：「居高位者易驕，處佚樂者易侈。
value.en: The emperor said, "Those who hold high rank easily grow arrogant, and those who live in comfort easily grow extravagant.
value.literal: The emperor said: "Those who dwell in high position easily become arrogant; those who dwell in ease and pleasure easily become extravagant.

value.zh: 驕則善言不入，而過不聞；
value.en: Arrogance shuts out good counsel so that faults go unheard;
value.literal: When arrogant, good words do not enter and faults are not heard;

value.zh: 侈則善道不立，而行不顧。
value.en: extravagance uproots the right path so that conduct is no longer restrained.
value.literal: when extravagant, the good Way is not established and conduct is not looked back upon.

value.zh: 如此者，未有不亡。
value.en: Rulers who fall into this have never failed to fall.
value.literal: Those like this—none have failed to perish.

value.zh: 卿言甚當。」
value.en: Your analysis is entirely apt."
value.literal: Your words are very apposite."

value.zh: 又論學術。
value.en: The conversation turned to learning and doctrine.
value.literal: They again discussed learning and doctrine.

value.zh: 安曰：「道不明，邪說害之也。」
value.en: An said, "When the Way is unclear, heretical teachings are to blame."
value.literal: An said: "When the Way is not clear, heterodox doctrines harm it."

value.zh: 帝曰：「邪說害道，猶美味之悅口，美色之眩目。
value.en: The emperor replied, "Heresy harms the Way as dainties please the palate and bright colors dazzle the eye.
value.literal: The emperor said: "Heterodox doctrines harming the Way are like delicacies pleasing the mouth and beautiful colors dazing the eyes.

value.zh: 邪說不去，則正道不興，天下何從治？」
value.en: Until heresy is cleared away the right Way cannot flourish—how can the realm be governed?"
value.literal: If heterodox doctrines are not removed, then the correct Way cannot rise—how would all under Heaven be governed from?"

value.zh: 安頓首曰：「陛下所言，可謂深探其本矣。」
value.en: An kowtowed and said, "Your Majesty has struck the very root of the matter."
value.literal: An knocked his head and said: "What Your Majesty has spoken may be called deeply probing its root."

value.zh: 安事帝十余歲，視諸儒最舊。
value.en: An had served the emperor for more than a decade and was the senior-most of the scholarly counselors.
value.literal: An had served the emperor more than ten years; among the various scholars he was the most senior.

value.zh: 及官侍從，寵愈渥。
value.en: Once he entered the inner circle of attendants, imperial favor only deepened.
value.literal: When he reached the office of attendant and follower, favor grew ever richer.

value.zh: 御制門帖子賜之曰：「國朝謀略無雙士，翰苑文章第一家。」
value.en: The emperor personally composed a couplet for his gate: "Unrivaled strategist of the dynasty; foremost writer of the academy."
value.literal: The emperor in his own hand composed a gate couplet and bestowed it on him, saying: "Of the dynasty's strategists, an unrivaled man; of the Hanlin garden's writings, the foremost family."

value.zh: 時人榮之。
value.en: Contemporaries regarded this as the highest honor.
value.literal: Men of the time took it as glory.

value.zh: 御史或言安隱過。
value.en: A censor reported that An had concealed misconduct.
value.literal: A censor at times spoke of An's hidden faults.

value.zh: 帝詰曰：「安寧有此，且若何從知？」
value.en: The emperor demanded, "Would An truly do such a thing—and how do you know?"
value.literal: The emperor interrogated: "Could An truly have this? Moreover, how did you come to know?"

value.zh: 曰：「聞之道路。」
value.en: The censor answered, "I heard it on the streets."
value.literal: He said: "I heard it on the road."

value.zh: 帝大怒，立黜之。
value.en: The emperor flew into a rage and had him dismissed on the spot.
value.literal: The emperor was greatly angry and immediately dismissed him.

value.zh: 張籌，字惟中，無錫人。
value.en: Zhang Chou, styled Weizhong, was from Wuxi.
value.literal: Zhang Chou, style name Weizhong, was a man of Wuxi.

value.zh: 父翼，嘗勸張士誠將莫天佑降，復請於平章胡美勿僇降人，城中人得完。
value.en: His father Zhang Yi had urged Zhang Shicheng to accept Mo Tianyou's surrender and persuaded Commissioner Hu Mei not to massacre the surrendered, sparing the city's population.
value.literal: His father Yi had once urged Zhang Shicheng to have Mo Tianyou submit, and again requested of Pacification Commissioner Hu Mei not to slaughter those who surrendered, so the people in the city were preserved intact.

value.zh: 以詹同薦，授翰林應奉，改禮部主事。
value.en: Recommended by Zhan Tong, he was appointed to respond to imperial compositions in the Hanlin Academy and later made a section chief in the Ministry of Rites.
value.literal: On Zhan Tong's recommendation he was appointed Hanlin Responding to Imperial Composition and changed to Ritual Department Section Chief.

value.zh: 奉詔與尚書陶凱編集漢、唐以來籓王事跡，為《歸鑒錄》。
value.en: By imperial order he and Minister Tao Kai compiled the deeds of feudal princes from Han and Tang onward into the Returning Mirror Record.
value.literal: By imperial command together with Minister Tao Kai he compiled deeds of feudal princes from Han and Tang onward, making the Returning Mirror Record.

value.zh: 洪武九年，由員外郎進尚書，與學士宋濂定諸王妃喪服之制。
value.en: In the ninth Hongwu year he rose from vice director to minister and, with Song Lian, set mourning regulations for princely consorts.
value.literal: In Hongwu year nine, from Vice Director he advanced to Minister and with Academician Song Lian fixed the mourning-garb system for various princely consorts.

value.zh: 籌記誦淹博，在禮曹久，諳於歷代禮文沿革。
value.en: Chou had a prodigious memory; after long service in the Ministry of Rites he knew the evolution of ritual texts through the ages.
value.literal: Chou's memory and recitation were broad and deep; long in the Ritual Office, he was thoroughly versed in the evolution of ritual texts through the ages.

value.zh: 然頗善附會。
value.en: Yet he was inclined to force classical texts to fit present needs.
value.literal: Yet he was rather good at forced interpretation.

value.zh: 初，陶安等定圜丘、方澤、宗廟、社稷諸儀，行數年矣。
value.en: Tao An and others had years earlier set rites for the Round Mound, Square Mound, ancestral temple, and state altars.
value.literal: At the beginning Tao An and others had fixed the rites of the Round Mound, Square Mound, ancestral temple, and state altar, and they had been practiced several years.

value.zh: 洪武九年，籌為尚書，乃更議合社稷為一壇，罷勾龍、棄配位，奉仁祖配饗，以明祖社尊而親之之道，遂以社稷與郊廟祀並列上祀。
value.en: As minister in the ninth year Chou merged the altars of soil and grain into one, removed Gou Long and Qi from associated worship, and enshrined the founding emperor's father there, elevating the state altars to the highest tier of sacrifice alongside suburban rites.
value.literal: In Hongwu year nine Chou became Minister and then again deliberated merging the state altars into one altar, abolishing the associated positions of Gou Long and Qi, offering the benevolent ancestor as associated sacrifice, to clarify the Way of honoring the state altars while treating them as kin—and thus placed the state altars in upper sacrifice alongside suburban and temple sacrifice.

value.zh: 識者竊非之。
value.en: Knowledgeable observers quietly disapproved.
value.literal: Men of insight privately disapproved.

value.zh: 已，出為湖廣參政。
value.en: He was soon posted as administrative commissioner of Huguang.
value.literal: Before long he went out as Administrative Commissioner of Huguang.

value.zh: 十年坐事罰輸作。
value.en: In the tenth year he was sentenced to corvée labor for an offense.
value.literal: In year ten for an offense he was penalized to perform labor service.

value.zh: 十二年仍起禮部員外郎。
value.en: In the twelfth year he was restored as vice director in the Ministry of Rites.
value.literal: In year twelve he was still raised as Ritual Department Vice Director.

value.zh: 後復官，以事免。
value.en: He was later reappointed but dismissed again after another incident.
value.literal: Later his office was restored again; for an affair he was dismissed.

value.zh: 劉三吾
value.en: Liu Sanwu
value.literal: Liu Sanwu

value.en: (Wang Rui and Zhu Shan)〉

value.zh: 吳伯宗
value.en: Wu Bozong

value.en: (Bao Xun and Ren Hengtai)〉

value.en: Wu Chen and Gui Yanliang
value.literal: Wu Chen, Gui Yanliang

value.literal: (Li Xiyan, Xu Zongshi, Chen Nanbin, Liu Chun, Dong Zizhuang, Zhao Jitong, Yang Fu, Jin Shi, and others)〉

value.en: Song Ne

value.en: (Xu Cunren, Zhang Meihe, Nie Xuan, and Bei Qiong)〉
value.literal: (Xu Cunren, Zhang Meihe, Nie Xuan, Bei Qiong)〉

value.zh: 趙俶
value.en: Zhao Chu
value.literal: Zhao Chu

value.zh: 〈（錢宰蕭執）〉
value.en: (Qian Zai and Xiao Zhi)〉
value.literal: (Qian Zai, Xiao Zhi)〉

value.zh: 李叔正劉崧羅復仁
value.en: Li Shuzheng, Liu Song, and Luo Furen
value.literal: Li Shuzheng, Liu Song, Luo Furen

value.zh: 〈（孫汝敬）〉
value.en: (Sun Rujing)〉
value.literal: (Sun Rujing)〉

value.zh: 趙俶，字本初，山陰人。
value.en: Zhao Chu, style name Benchu, was a native of Shanyin.
value.literal: Zhao Chu, style name Benchu, was a native of Shanyin.

value.zh: 元進士。
value.en: He was a jinshi graduate of the Yuan dynasty.
value.literal: A Yuan-dynasty jinshi graduate.

value.zh: 洪武六年，征授國子博士。
value.en: In the sixth year of Hongwu he was summoned and appointed erudite at the Directorate of the National University.
value.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu, he was summoned and appointed Erudite at the Directorate of the National University.

value.zh: 帝嘗禦奉天殿，召俶及錢宰、貝瓊等曰：「汝等一以孔子所定經書為教，慎勿雜蘇秦、張儀縱橫之言。」
value.en: The Emperor once held court in the Hall of Upholding Heaven and summoned Chu, Qian Zai, Bei Qiong, and others, saying, "You must teach only the classics established by Confucius as your teaching. Be careful not to introduce the stratagem rhetoric of Su Qin and Zhang Yi."
value.literal: The Emperor once held court in the Hall of Upholding Heaven, summoned Chu along with Qian Zai, Bei Qiong, and others, and said: "You shall take exclusively the classics established by Confucius as your teaching; be careful not to mix in the stratagem rhetoric of Su Qin and Zhang Yi."

value.zh: 諸臣頓首受命。
value.en: The officials all kowtowed and accepted the command.
value.literal: The officials all kowtowed and accepted the command.

value.zh: 俶因請頒正定《十三經》於天下，屏《戰國策》及陰陽讖卜諸書，勿列學宮。
value.en: Chu then asked that the corrected 《Thirteen Classics》 be promulgated throughout the realm, and that the 《Strategies of the Warring States》 together with works on yin-yang lore, prophecy, and divination be barred from the academies.
value.literal: Chu thereupon requested that the corrected 《Thirteen Classics》 be promulgated throughout the realm, and that the 《Strategies of the Warring States》 together with books on yin-yang lore, prophecy, and divination be excluded and not placed in the academies.

value.zh: 明年擇諸生穎異者三十五人，命俶專領之，教以古文。
value.en: The following year thirty-five exceptionally gifted students were chosen, and Chu was ordered to take charge of them and teach them ancient-style prose.
value.literal: The next year thirty-five outstanding students were selected, and Chu was ordered to take charge of them exclusively and teach them ancient-style prose.

value.zh: 尋擢李擴、黃義等入文華、武英二堂說書，皆見用。
value.en: Soon Li Kuo, Huang Yi, and others were promoted to lecture in the Wenhua and Wuying halls, and all were put to use.
value.literal: Soon Li Kuo, Huang Yi, and others were promoted to lecture in the Wenhua and Wuying halls, and all were employed.

value.zh: 九年，御史臺言：「博士俶以《詩經》教成均四年，其弟子多為方嶽重臣及持節各部者。
value.en: In the ninth year the Censorate reported, "Erudite Chu has taught the 《Classic of Poetry》 at the Imperial Academy for four years, and many of his disciples have become leading provincial ministers and imperial envoys in various departments.
value.literal: In the ninth year the Censorate reported: "Erudite Chu has taught the 《Classic of Poetry》 at the Imperial Academy for four years; many of his disciples have become great ministers of provincial governors and envoys holding imperial insignia in various departments.

value.zh: 今年逾懸車，請賜骸骨。」
value.en: This year he has passed the age of retirement and asks to be permitted to return home."
value.literal: This year he has passed the age for retiring, and requests to be granted leave to return his bones."

value.zh: 於是以翰林院待制致仕，賜內帑錢治裝。
value.en: Thereupon he retired with the title of Hanlin attendant draftsman and was granted money from the inner treasury for his journey home.
value.literal: Thereupon he retired with the title Hanlin Academy Attendant Draftsman and was granted money from the inner treasury for travel expenses.

value.zh: 宋濂率同官暨諸生千余人送之。
value.en: Song Lian led more than a thousand fellow officials and students to see him off.
value.literal: Song Lian led more than a thousand fellow officials and students to see him off.

value.zh: 卒年八十一。
value.en: He died at the age of eighty-one.
value.literal: He died at the age of eighty-one.

value.zh: 子圭玉，兵部侍郎，出知萊州，有聲。
value.en: His son Guiyu became vice minister of war and went out to serve as prefect of Laizhou, where he earned a fine reputation.
value.literal: His son Guiyu became Vice Minister of War and went out to serve as Prefect of Laizhou, where he won renown.

value.zh: 明太祖既定江左，鑒前代之失，置宦者不及百人。
value.en: Once the Ming founder had consolidated his hold on the lower Yangzi, he studied the mistakes of earlier dynasties and kept the number of eunuchs to under a hundred.
value.literal: After the Ming founder had secured the lower Yangzi, he took warning from the failings of earlier dynasties and kept fewer than a hundred eunuchs.

value.zh: 迨末年頒《祖訓》，乃定為十有二監及各司局，稍稱備員矣。
value.en: By the end of his reign, when he promulgated the Ancestral Injunctions, the establishment was fixed at twelve directorates and the various bureaus—barely enough to count as a full complement.
value.literal: By the end of his reign, when he issued the Ancestral Injunctions, they were fixed at twelve directorates and various offices, and could only just be said to be fully staffed.

value.zh: 然定制，不得兼外臣文武銜，不得御外臣冠服，官無過四品，月米一石，衣食於內庭。
value.en: Yet the standing regulations barred them from holding concurrent civil or military titles in the outer administration, from wearing the headgear and robes of outer ministers, and from rising above the fourth rank; they received one picul of rice a month and were clothed and fed within the inner palace.
value.literal: But the established regulations forbade them from holding civilian or military titles outside the inner court, from wearing the hats and robes of outer ministers, and limited their rank to no higher than the fourth; they received one dan of rice a month and were housed and fed in the inner palace.

value.zh: 嘗鐫鐵牌置宮門曰：「內臣不得干預政事，預者斬。」
value.en: He once had an iron plaque engraved and placed at the palace gate, saying: "Inner servants must not interfere in government affairs; anyone who does so shall be executed."
value.literal: He once had an iron plaque engraved and placed at the palace gate, saying: "Inner servants must not interfere in government affairs; anyone who does so shall be executed."

value.zh: 敕諸司不得與文移往來。
value.en: He also ordered the various ministries not to exchange official correspondence with them.
value.literal: He also ordered the various offices not to exchange written documents with them.

value.zh: 有老閹供事久，一日從容語及政事，帝大怒，即日斥還鄉。
value.en: An old eunuch who had long served at court once spoke casually about state affairs; the emperor flew into a rage and sent him home that very day.
value.literal: There was an old eunuch who had long served the court; one day he spoke casually about government affairs, and the emperor was furious and expelled him back to his hometown that same day.

value.zh: 嘗用杜安道為御用監。
value.en: He once appointed Du Andao director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.
value.literal: He once employed Du Andao as Director of Imperial Services.

value.zh: 安道，外臣也，以鑷工侍帝數十年，帷幄計議皆與知，性縝密不泄，過諸大臣前一揖不啟口而退。
value.en: Andao was an outer subject who had served the emperor for decades as a metalworker; he was privy to every plan and deliberation in the field camp, was meticulous and tight-lipped by nature, and whenever he passed the senior ministers he would bow once and withdraw without a word.
value.literal: Andao was a commoner who served the emperor for several decades as a maker of tweezers; he was privy to all the plans and deliberations in the tented camp, was by nature meticulous and secretive, and whenever he passed the great ministers he would bow once and leave without saying a word.

value.zh: 太祖愛之，然亡他寵異，後遷出為光祿寺卿。
value.en: The founder held him in esteem but granted him no further extraordinary favor; later he was transferred out to serve as minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
value.literal: The Ming founder favored him, but did not grant him any other special favor; later he was transferred out as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

value.zh: 有趙成者，洪武八年以內侍使河州市馬。
value.en: There was also Zhao Cheng, whom in the eighth year of Hongwu the court sent as an inner attendant to purchase horses in Hezhou.
value.literal: There was one Zhao Cheng; in the eighth year of Hongwu he was sent as an inner attendant to buy horses in Hezhou.

value.zh: 其後以市馬出者，又有司禮監慶童等，然皆不敢有所干竊。
value.en: Later others were sent out on horse-buying missions as well, including Qingtong of the Directorate of Ceremonial—but none of them dared to meddle in affairs or steal.
value.literal: Later there were also those sent out to buy horses, such as Qingtong of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service, but none of them dared to meddle or pilfer anything.

value.zh: 建文帝嗣位，御內臣益嚴，詔出外稍不法，許有司械聞。
value.en: When the Jianwen Emperor came to the throne, he tightened control over the inner servants still further, decreeing that if any of them went outside and committed even minor offenses, local officials might arrest them and report the matter.
value.literal: When the Jianwen Emperor succeeded to the throne, he tightened control over the inner servants even more severely; he issued an edict that if any of them went outside and committed even minor offenses, the local authorities were permitted to arrest and report them.

value.zh: 及燕師逼江北，內臣多逃入其軍，漏朝廷虛實。
value.en: When the Prince of Yan's army pressed to the north bank of the Yangzi, many inner servants deserted into his ranks and betrayed the court's strengths and weaknesses.
value.literal: When the Yan army pressed against the north bank of the Yangzi, many inner servants fled into its ranks and leaked the court's weaknesses.

value.zh: 文皇以為忠於己，而狗兒輩復以軍功得幸，即位後遂多所委任。
value.en: The Yongle Emperor regarded them as loyal to his cause, and men such as Dog'er won further favor through military service; once he took the throne, he entrusted them with ever wider responsibilities.
value.literal: The Yongle Emperor considered them loyal to him, and Gou'er and the others were further favored because of military merit; once he came to the throne, he entrusted them with many responsibilities.

value.zh: 永樂元年，內官監李興奉敕往勞暹羅國王。
value.en: In the first year of Yongle, Li Xing of the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs was ordered to travel to Siam and convey the emperor's condolences to its king.
value.literal: In the first year of Yongle, the inner-court official Li Xing was ordered to go and present condolences to the king of Siam.

value.zh: 三年，遣太監鄭和帥舟師下西洋。
value.en: In the third year the court dispatched the eunuch Zheng He to lead a fleet on the voyage to the Western Ocean.
value.literal: In the third year, Zheng He was sent with a fleet as envoy to the Western Ocean.

value.zh: 八年，都督譚青營有內官王安等。
value.en: In the eighth year inner officials such as Wang An were attached to the camp of the regional commander Tan Qing.
value.literal: In the eighth year, at General Tan Qing's camp there were inner officials such as Wang An.

value.zh: 又命馬靖鎮甘肅，馬騏鎮交阯。
value.en: He also ordered Ma Jing to take command in Gansu and Ma Qi to take command in Jiaozhi.
value.literal: He also ordered Ma Jing to garrison Gansu and Ma Qi to garrison Jiaozhi.

value.zh: 十八年置東廠，令刺事。
value.en: In the eighteenth year the Eastern Depot was set up and charged with intelligence gathering.
value.literal: In the eighteenth year the Eastern Depot was established and ordered to investigate matters.

value.zh: 蓋明世宦官出使、專征、監軍、分鎮、刺臣民隱事諸大權，皆自永樂間始。
value.en: Thus the great powers later wielded by eunuchs—diplomatic missions abroad, independent military campaigns, supervision of armies, regional commands, and surveillance of ministers and commoners—all had their beginning in the Yongle reign.
value.literal: The great powers exercised by eunuchs in foreign missions, independent campaigns, military supervision, regional garrisons, and spying on the hidden affairs of ministers and commoners all began in the Yongle years.

value.zh: 當是時，瑾權擅天下，威福任情。
value.en: In those days Jin wielded sole power over the empire, dispensing favor and punishment entirely as he pleased.
value.literal: At that time Jin held power over the whole realm and dispensed favor and punishment as he wished.

value.zh: 有罪人溺水死，乃坐御史匡翼之罪。
value.en: When a criminal drowned, the censor Kuang Yizhi was punished for it.
value.literal: When a criminal drowned and died, the blame was placed on the censor Kuang Yizhi.

value.zh: 嘗求學士吳儼賄，不得，又聽都御史劉宇讒，怒御史楊南金，乃以大計外吏奏中，落二人職。
value.en: He once demanded a bribe from academician Wu Yan and did not get it; then, heeding the slander of Grand Censor Liu Yu, he turned on censor Yang Nanjin and, in the annual evaluation of outside officials, had both men removed from office.
value.literal: He once sought a bribe from the scholar Wu Yan and got none; then, listening to the slander of Grand Censor Liu Yu, he became angry with the censor Yang Nanjin and used the annual evaluation of outside officials to have the two of them removed from office.

value.zh: 授播州土司楊斌為四川按察使。
value.en: He appointed Yang Bin, a native chieftain of Bozhou, surveillance commissioner of Sichuan.
value.literal: He appointed Yang Bin, a native chief of Bozhou, as Sichuan surveillance commissioner.

value.zh: 令奴婿閭潔督山東學政。
value.en: He put his son-in-law Lü Jie in charge of the school administration of Shandong.
value.literal: He ordered his son-in-law Lü Jie to supervise the school administration of Shandong.

value.zh: 公侯勛戚以下，莫敢鈞禮，每私謁，相率跪拜。
value.en: From dukes, marquises, meritorious nobles, and imperial in-laws downward, none dared insist on equal courtesy; whenever they paid a private visit, they knelt and bowed in succession.
value.literal: Dukes, marquises, meritorious officers, and relatives by marriage all dared not insist on equal courtesy; whenever they paid a private visit, they all knelt and bowed in turn.

value.zh: 章奏先具紅揭投瑾，號紅本，然後上通政司，號白本，皆稱劉太監而不名。
value.en: Memorials had first to be prepared on red paper and submitted to Jin—the "red memorials"—and only afterward sent on to the Directorate of Communications as "white memorials"; everywhere he was addressed as Eunuch Liu, never by name.
value.literal: Memorials had first to be prepared as red slips and submitted to Jin, known as the red memorials; only then were they sent on to the Court of State Affairs as white memorials. In all cases he was called Eunuch Liu and not by name.

value.zh: 都察院奏讞誤名瑾，瑾怒詈之，都御史屠滽率屬跪謝乃已。
value.en: When the Censorate named Jin in a judgment report by mistake, he flew into a rage and cursed them; Grand Censor Tu Yong and his subordinates had to kneel and apologize before he would let the matter drop.
value.literal: When the Censorate referred to Jin by name in a judgment report, Jin cursed them in anger, and Grand Censor Tu Yong and his subordinates had to kneel and apologize before he stopped.

value.zh: 遣使察核邊倉，都御史周南、張鼐、馬中錫、湯全、劉憲，布政以下官孫祿、冒政、方矩、華福、金獻民、劉遜、郭緒、張翼，郎中劉繹、王藎等，並以赦前罪，下獄追補邊粟，憲至瘐死。
value.en: He sent envoys to audit the border granaries, and Grand Censors Zhou Nan, Zhang Nai, Ma Zhongxi, Tang Quan, and Liu Xian, along with provincial administrators Sun Lu, Mao Zheng, Fang Ju, Hua Fu, Jin Xianmin, Liu Xun, Guo Xu, Zhang Yi, and secretaries Liu Yi and Wang Jin, were all imprisoned on pre-amnesty offenses and forced to make restitution in border grain; Liu Xian died of illness in prison.
value.literal: He sent envoys to inspect the border granaries, and Grand Censors Zhou Nan, Zhang Nai, Ma Zhongxi, Tang Quan, and Liu Xian, along with the provincial officials Sun Lu, Mao Zheng, Fang Ju, Hua Fu, Jin Xianmin, Liu Xun, Guo Xu, Zhang Yi, and the ministry officials Liu Yi, Wang Jin, and others, were all imprisoned for crimes supposedly covered by amnesty and made to repay border grain; Xian died in prison of illness.

value.zh: 又察鹽課，杖巡鹽御史王潤，逮前運使寧舉、楊奇等。
value.en: He also inspected the salt revenues, flogged salt censor Wang Run, and arrested former transport commissioners Ning Ju, Yang Qi, and others.
value.literal: He also inspected the salt revenues, flogged the salt-surveillance censor Wang Run, and arrested the former transport commissioners Ning Ju and Yang Qi and others.

value.zh: 察內甲字庫，謫尚書王佐以下百七十三人。
value.en: He inspected the Inner Armor and Character Treasury and demoted one hundred seventy-three officials, including Minister Wang Zuo.
value.literal: He inspected the Inner Armor Character Treasury and demoted 173 people, including Minister Wang Zuo.

value.zh: 復創罰米法，嘗忤瑾者，皆擿發輸邊。
value.en: He revived the penalty of grain fines as well; anyone who had ever offended Jin was hunted out and made to deliver grain to the border.
value.literal: He also invented the penalty of grain fines again; anyone who had offended Jin was all exposed and sent to the frontier.

value.zh: 故尚書雍泰、馬文升、劉大夏、韓文、許進，都御史楊一清、李進、王忠，侍郎張縉，給事中趙士賢，任良弼，御史張津，陳順、喬恕、聶賢、曹來旬等數十人悉破家，死者繫其妻孥。
value.en: Thus former ministers Yun Tai, Ma Wensheng, Liu Daxia, Han Wen, and Xu Jin; Grand Censors Yang Yiqing, Li Jin, and Wang Zhong; Vice Minister Zhang Jin; assistant secretaries Zhao Shixian and Ren Liangbi; censors Zhang Jin, Chen Shun, Qiao Shou, Nie Xian, Cao Laixun, and dozens more were ruined; where the accused died, their wives and children were held liable as well.
value.literal: Thus ministers such as Yun Tai, Ma Wensheng, Liu Daxia, Han Wen, and Xu Jin; Grand Censors Yang Yiqing, Li Jin, and Wang Zhong; Vice Ministers Zhang Jin; Assistant Secretaries Zhao Shixian and Ren Liangbi; censors Zhang Jin, Chen Shun, Qiao Shou, Nie Xian, Cao Laixun, and dozens of others all lost their homes, and those who died left their wives and children bound up with them.

value.zh: 姚安鶴慶武定尋甸麗江元江永昌新化威遠北勝灣甸鎮康大侯瀾滄衛麓川
value.en: Yao'an, Heqing, Wuding, Xundian, Lijiang, Yuanjiang, Yongchang, Xinhua, Weiyuan, Beisheng, Wandian, Zhenkang, Dahou, Lancang Guard, and Luchuan
value.literal: Yao'an, Heqing, Wuding, Xundian, Lijiang, Yuanjiang, Yongchang, Xinhua, Weiyuan, Beisheng, Wandian, Zhenkang, Dahou, Lancang Guard, Luchuan

value.zh: 洪武六年遣使田儼、程鬥南、張祎、錢允恭賫詔往諭。
value.en: In Hongwu 6 the envoys Tian Yan, Cheng Dou'nan, Zhang Yi, and Qian Yonggong were sent with an imperial edict to announce the court's will.
value.literal: In Hongwu 6 envoys Tian Yan, Cheng Dou'nan, Zhang Yi, and Qian Yonggong were dispatched bearing an imperial edict to announce the imperial will.

value.zh: 至安南，留二年，以道阻不通。
value.en: They reached Annam and stayed there two years, the road ahead blocked and impassable.
value.literal: They reached Annam and remained two years, as the route was blocked and impassable.

value.zh: 有詔召之，惟儼還，余皆道卒。
value.en: An edict recalled them; only Tian Yan made it back—the others all died on the journey.
value.literal: An edict summoned them back; only Tian Yan returned—the rest all died on the road.

value.zh: 十五年，大兵下雲南，進以大理，下金齒。
value.en: In the fifteenth year the main army swept into Yunnan, pushed through Dali, and captured Jinchi.
value.literal: In the fifteenth year the grand army descended on Yunnan, advanced through Dali, and took Jinchi.

value.zh: 平緬與金齒壤地相接，土蠻思倫發聞之懼，遂降。
value.en: Ping Mian bordered Jinchi directly; when the native chieftain Si Lunfa heard the news he was terrified and submitted.
value.literal: Ping Mian shared a border with Jinchi; the tribal chieftain Si Lunfa heard of this and, fearing attack, submitted.

value.zh: 因置平緬宣慰使司，以倫發為宣慰使。
value.en: A Ping Mian Pacification Commission was accordingly established, and Lunfa was appointed its pacification commissioner.
value.literal: A Ping Mian Pacification Commission was therefore established, with Lunfa appointed pacification commissioner.

value.zh: 十七年八月，倫發遣刀令孟獻方物，並上元所授宣慰使司印。
value.en: In the eighth month of the seventeenth year Lunfa sent Dao Lingmeng with local tribute and the Yuan-granted seal of the pacification commission.
value.literal: In the eighth month of the seventeenth year, Lunfa sent Dao Lingmeng to present local products and surrender the seal of the pacification commission granted by the Yuan.

value.zh: 詔改平緬宣慰使為平緬軍民宣慰使司，並賜倫發朝服、冠帶及織金文綺、鈔錠。
value.en: An edict reorganized the commission as the Ping Mian Military-Civilian Pacification Commission and granted Lunfa court robes, cap and belt, brocaded gold-thread silk, and banknotes.
value.literal: An edict changed the Ping Mian Pacification Commission to the Ping Mian Military-Civilian Pacification Commission, and Lunfa was granted court robes, cap and belt, brocaded gold-thread silk, and ingots of paper money.

value.zh: 尋改平緬軍民宣慰使司為麓川平緬軍民宣慰使司。
value.en: It was soon renamed the Luchuan-Ping Mian Military-Civilian Pacification Commission.
value.literal: Soon the Ping Mian Military-Civilian Pacification Commission was renamed the Luchuan-Ping Mian Military-Civilian Pacification Commission.

value.zh: 麓川與平緬連境，元時分置兩路以統其所部，至是以倫發遣使貢，命兼統麓川之地。
value.en: Luchuan and Ping Mian were adjacent; the Yuan had divided them into two circuits to govern their peoples separately. Now, because Lunfa had sent tribute envoys, he was ordered to govern Luchuan as well.
value.literal: Luchuan and Ping Mian shared a border; under the Yuan two circuits had been separately established to govern their respective territories. Now, because Lunfa had dispatched envoys with tribute, he was ordered to govern Luchuan as well.

value.zh: 先主 劉備
value.en: The Former Lord: Liu Bei.
value.literal: The Former Lord Liu Bei.

value.zh: 二十五年，魏文帝稱尊號，改年曰黃初。
value.en: In the twenty-fifth year Cao Pi of Wei took the imperial title and changed the era name to Huangchu.
value.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Wei Emperor Wen assumed honored title; changed the year to Huangchu.

value.zh: 或傳聞漢帝見害，先主乃發喪制服，追諡曰孝愍皇帝。
value.en: Rumors spread that the Han emperor had been murdered; Liu Bei then went into mourning and posthumously titled him Emperor Xiaomin.
value.literal: Some heard rumor the Han emperor was seen harmed; the Former Lord then issued mourning and donned mourning garments; posthumously titled Filial Compassionate Emperor.

value.zh: 是後在所並言眾瑞，日月相屬，故議郎陽泉侯劉豹、青衣侯向舉、偏將軍張裔、黃權、大司馬屬殷純、益州別駕從事趙莋、治中從事楊洪、從事祭酒何宗、議曹從事杜瓊、勸學從事張爽、尹默、譙周等上言：
value.en: Thenceforth every district reported omens in endless succession; Gentleman-adviser Liu Bao, marquis of Yangquan, Xiang Ju, marquis of Qingyi, Major General Zhang Yi, Huang Quan, Yin Chun of the grand marshal’s staff, chief clerk Zhao Zha, headquarters clerk Yang Hong, libationer He Zong, Du Qiong of the consult bureau, Zhang Shuang, Yin Mo, Qiao Zhou, and others memorialized:
value.literal: After this in places together spoke many auspices, sun and moon linked in succession; therefore Gentleman-adviser village marquis of Yangquan Liu Bao, village marquis of Qingyi Xiang Ju, major general Zhang Yi, Huang Quan, Grand Marshal’s subordinate Yin Chun, Yizhou chief clerk Zhao Zha, headquarters clerk Yang Hong, clerk libationer He Zong, consult bureau clerk Du Qiong, encourage-learning clerk Zhang Shuang, Yin Mo, Qiao Zhou and others upward spoke:

value.zh: 關羽字雲長，本字長生，河東解人也。
value.en: Guan Yu, styled Yunzhang—his original style was Changsheng—came from Jie in Hedong.
value.literal: Guan Yu, courtesy name Yunzhang, originally courtesy name Changsheng, was a native of Jie in Hedong.

value.zh: 亡命奔涿郡。
value.en: He fled the law and made his way to Zhuo commandery.
value.literal: He fled as an outlaw and ran to Zhuo commandery.

value.zh: 先主於鄉里合徒眾，而羽與張飛為之禦侮。
value.en: While the First Lord was raising a band of men in his home country, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei stood as his shield against abuse and attack.
value.literal: When the First Lord gathered followers in his home district, Yu together with Zhang Fei defended him from insult and harm.

value.zh: 先主為平原相，以羽、飛為別部司馬，分統部曲。
value.en: Once the First Lord was appointed Administrator of Pingyuan, he made Guan Yu and Zhang Fei Separate Command Majors, splitting the command of their forces between them.
value.literal: When the First Lord became Administrator of Pingyuan, he appointed Yu and Fei as Separate Command Majors, each commanding a division of troops.

value.zh: 先主與二人寢則同床，恩若兄弟。
value.en: The First Lord slept on the same couch with the two of them, and the affection among them was like that of brothers.
value.literal: The First Lord with the two of them, when sleeping, shared one bed; their kindness was like that of brothers.

value.zh: 而稠人廣坐，侍立終日，隨先主周旋，不避艱險。
value.en: Even in thronged halls and before large assemblies they would stand attendance the whole day through, attending the First Lord wherever he went, never shrinking from hardship or peril.
value.literal: Yet in crowded places and at public gatherings they stood in attendance all day, following the First Lord in his comings and goings, not shunning hardship or danger.

value.zh: 〈蜀記曰：曹公與劉備圍呂布於下邳，關羽啟公，布使秦宜祿行求救，乞娶其妻，公許之。
value.en: 〈The Shu Ji records that when Lord Cao and Liu Bei had Lü Bu bottled up at Xiapi, Guan Yu petitioned him: Lü Bu had sent Qin Yilu out to plead for help, and Guan Yu asked leave to take Qin's wife in marriage; Lord Cao agreed.
value.literal: 〈The Shu Ji states: Lord Cao and Liu Bei besieged Lü Bu at Xiapi. Guan Yu reported to the Lord that, when Lü Bu had Qin Yilu go out to seek rescue, he begged to marry Qin's wife, and the Lord granted it.

value.zh: 臨破，又屢啟於公。
value.en: When the city was on the verge of being taken, he pressed the matter again and again with Lord Cao.
value.literal: As the city was about to fall, he repeatedly reported to the Lord.

value.zh: 公疑其有異色，先遣迎看，因自留之，羽心不自安。
value.en: Lord Cao suspected the woman was strikingly beautiful, sent someone ahead to fetch and inspect her, then kept her for himself—leaving Guan Yu uneasy in his mind.
value.literal: The Lord suspected she had unusual beauty, first sent men to meet and look at her, and therefore kept her himself; Yu's heart was not at ease.

value.zh: 此與魏氏春秋所說無異也。〉
value.en: This matches the account given in the Wei shi chunqiu.〉
value.literal: This is no different from what the Wei shi chunqiu says.〉

value.zh: 先主之襲殺徐州刺史車胄，使羽守下邳城，行太守事，
value.en: When the First Lord struck down Xu Province Inspector Che Zhou in a surprise attack, he left Guan Yu to hold Xiapi and conduct the duties of Administrator.
value.literal: When the First Lord suddenly attacked and killed the Inspector of Xu Province, Che Zhou, he had Yu guard Xiapi city and act as Administrator.

value.zh: 〈《魏書》云：以羽領徐州。〉
value.en: 〈The Wei shu adds that Guan Yu was given authority over Xu Province.〉
value.literal: 〈The Wei shu states: Yu was placed in charge of Xu Province.〉

value.zh: 而身還小沛。
value.en: The First Lord himself meanwhile withdrew to Xiao Pei.
value.literal: While he himself returned to Xiao Pei.

value.zh: 先主自葭萌還攻劉璋，召諸葛亮。
value.en: The First Lord marched back from Jiameng against Liu Zhang and called up Zhuge Liang.
value.literal: The First Lord returned from Jiameng to attack Liu Zhang and summoned Zhuge Liang.

value.zh: 亮率雲與張飛等俱溯江西上，平定郡縣。
value.en: Zhuge Liang took Zhao Yun, Zhang Fei, and the rest up the river westward, reducing counties as they went.
value.literal: Liang led Yun together with Zhang Fei and others alike upriver west, pacifying commanderies and districts.

value.zh: 至江州，分遣雲從外水上江陽，與亮會於成都。
value.en: At Jiangzhou he detached Zhao Yun up the outer water route to Jiangyang to rendezvous with Zhuge Liang at Chengdu.
value.literal: Reaching Jiangzhou, he separately dispatched Yun from the outer waters up to Jiangyang to meet Liang at Chengdu.

value.zh: 成都既定，以雲為翊軍將軍。
value.en: Once Chengdu was secure, he named Zhao Yun General Who Aids the Army.
value.literal: When Chengdu was settled, he made Yun General Who Aids the Army.

value.zh: 雲別傳曰：益州既定，時議欲以成都中屋舍及城外園地桑田分賜諸將。
value.en: The Zhao Yun biezhuan records that after Yizhou was pacified, some proposed dividing Chengdu houses and suburban gardens and mulberry fields among the generals.
value.literal: The Zhao Yun biezhuan states: When Yizhou was settled, at the time there was discussion of wanting to divide and grant to the various generals the houses within Chengdu and the garden lands and mulberry fields outside the walls.

value.zh: 雲駮之曰：「霍去病以匈奴未滅，無用家為，令國賊非但匈奴，未可求安也。
value.en: Zhao Yun objected: "Huo Qubing said that while the Xiongnu still lived, a man had no business building a home; our state's foe is not the Xiongnu alone—we cannot settle into comfort yet.
value.literal: Yun rebutted, saying, "Huo Qubing, because the Xiongnu were not yet destroyed, had no use for a home; now the state's enemy is not only the Xiongnu—one cannot seek ease.

value.zh: 須天下都定，各反桑梓，歸耕本土，乃其宜耳。
value.en: Only when the realm is wholly at peace should each man return home and till his own fields—that is the proper course.
value.literal: Only when all under Heaven is fully settled should each return to his native place and go back to farm his homeland—that is fitting.

value.zh: 益州人民，初罹兵革，田宅皆可歸還，今安居複業，然後可役調，得其歡心。」
value.en: The people of Yizhou have only just endured war; their fields and homes should be restored. Let them settle and resume their livelihoods first—only then levy service and taxes and win their goodwill."
value.literal: The people of Yizhou had just suffered war; fields and dwellings can all be returned; now let them settle and resume their occupations, and only then can levies and corvée be imposed to win their hearts."

value.zh: 先主即從之。
value.en: The First Lord accepted the advice at once.
value.literal: The First Lord at once followed this advice.

value.zh: 夏侯淵敗，曹公爭漢中地，運米北山下，數千萬囊。
value.en: After Xiahou Yuan's defeat, Lord Cao fought for Hanzhong and hauled grain in tens of millions of sacks to the foot of North Mountain.
value.literal: Xiahou Yuan was defeated; Lord Cao contested Hanzhong territory and transported grain to the foot of North Mountain—tens of millions of sacks.

value.zh: 黃忠以為可取，雲兵隨忠取米。
value.en: Huang Zhong judged the stores ripe for the taking, and Zhao Yun's men went with him to seize the grain.
value.literal: Huang Zhong thought it could be taken; Yun's troops followed Zhong to seize the grain.

value.zh: 忠過期不還，雲將數十騎輕行出圍，迎視忠等。
value.en: When Huang Zhong failed to return on time, Zhao Yun took a few dozen horsemen on a swift ride out of camp to find him.
value.literal: When Zhong passed the deadline and did not return, Yun led several dozen horsemen on a light sortie out of the encampment to meet and look in on Zhong and the others.

value.zh: 值曹公揚兵大出，雲為公前鋒所擊，方戰，其大眾至，勢偪，遂前突其陳，且鬥且卻。
value.en: Lord Cao marched out in strength; Zhao Yun collided with the vanguard and, as the main host closed in, drove into the enemy line while fighting his way back.
value.literal: He encountered Lord Cao raising troops and coming out in force; Yun was struck by the Lord's vanguard. As he was fighting, the enemy's main force arrived; the situation pressed hard, so he charged forward into their formation, fighting as he retreated.

value.zh: 公軍散，已復合，雲陷敵，還趣圍。
value.en: The Wei ranks broke, then re-formed; Zhao Yun was trapped among the enemy and wheeled back toward his camp.
value.literal: The Lord's army scattered, then rallied again; Yun was cut off among the enemy and turned back toward the encampment.

value.zh: 將張著被創，雲復馳馬還營迎著。
value.en: General Zhang Zhu was wounded, and Zhao Yun galloped back into camp to bring him out.
value.literal: General Zhang Zhu was wounded; Yun again galloped back to camp to receive Zhu.

value.zh: 公軍追至圍，此時沔陽長張翼在雲圍內，翼欲閉門拒守，而雲入營，更大開門，偃旗息鼓。
value.en: Wei troops pressed to the stockade. Zhang Yi, magistrate of Mianyang, was inside and meant to shut the gates; Zhao Yun entered, threw the gates wide, lowered the banners, and silenced the drums.
value.literal: The Lord's army pursued to the encampment. At that time Zhang Yi, magistrate of Mianyang, was inside Yun's encampment and wished to close the gate and hold in defense; but Yun entered the camp and instead opened the gate wide, lowered the banners, and silenced the drums.

value.zh: 公軍疑雲有伏兵，引去。
value.en: The Wei army suspected an ambush and withdrew.
value.literal: The Lord's army suspected Yun had ambush troops and withdrew.

value.zh: 雲雷鼓震天，惟以戎弩於後射公軍，公軍驚駭，自相蹂踐，墮漢水中死者甚多。
value.en: Zhao Yun rolled the drums to heaven and raked the retreating Wei ranks with crossbows from the rear; panic broke their lines, and many drowned in the Han River.
value.literal: Yun thundered the drums to shake heaven and with crossbows alone shot at the Lord's army from behind; the Lord's army was shocked and terrified, trampled one another, and many fell into the Han River and died.

value.zh: 先主明旦自來至雲營圍視昨戰處，曰：「子龍一身都是膽也。」
value.en: The next morning the First Lord came in person to Zhao Yun's camp to see the field of battle and said, "Zilong is courage from head to foot."
value.literal: The next morning the First Lord came in person to Yun's encampment to view yesterday's battlefield and said, "Zilong's whole body is courage."

value.zh: 作樂飲宴至暝，軍中號雲為虎威將軍。
value.en: There was music and feasting until dusk, and the army styled Zhao Yun General Who Displays Tiger Might.
value.literal: Music was made and a banquet held until dusk; in the army Yun was styled General Who Displays Tiger Might.

value.zh: 孫權襲荊州，先主大怒，欲討權。
value.en: When Sun Quan seized Jing Province, the First Lord was furious and meant to march against him.
value.literal: Sun Quan raided Jing Province; the First Lord was greatly enraged and wished to campaign against Quan.

value.zh: 雲諫曰：「國賊是曹操，非孫權也，且先滅魏，則吳自服。
value.en: Zhao Yun remonstrated: "The state's enemy is Cao Cao, not Sun Quan. Destroy Wei first and Wu will submit of itself.
value.literal: Yun remonstrated, saying, "The state's enemy is Cao Cao, not Sun Quan; moreover, if Wei is destroyed first, then Wu will submit of itself.

value.zh: 操身雖斃，子丕篡盜，當因眾心，早圖關中，居河、渭上流以討凶逆，關東義士必裹糧策馬以迎王師。
value.en: Though Cao Cao is dead, his son Pi has usurped the throne. Seize the people's will, take Guanzhong early, hold the upper He and Wei, and march against the traitors—the righteous east of the Pass will saddle up with grain to welcome the royal army.
value.literal: Though Cao's person has perished, his son Pi usurped and stole the throne; one should follow the people's hearts, plan early for Guanzhong, hold the upper reaches of the He and Wei rivers to campaign against the traitors, and the righteous men east of the Pass will surely wrap grain and spur their horses to welcome the royal army.

value.zh: 不應置魏，先與吳戰；
value.en: Do not set Wei aside to fight Wu first;
value.literal: One should not set Wei aside and fight Wu first;

value.zh: 兵勢一交，不得卒解。」
value.en: once arms are joined, the war cannot quickly be ended."
value.literal: once military momentum is joined, it cannot be quickly resolved."

value.zh: 先主不聽，遂東征，留雲督江州。
value.en: The First Lord would not listen and marched east, leaving Zhao Yun to oversee Jiangzhou.
value.literal: The First Lord did not heed this and thereupon campaigned east, leaving Yun to oversee Jiangzhou.

value.zh: 先主失利於秭歸，雲進兵至永安，吳軍已退。
value.en: After the First Lord's defeat at Zigui, Zhao Yun advanced to Yong'an and found the Wu army already gone.
value.literal: The First Lord met defeat at Zigui; Yun advanced to Yong'an and the Wu army had already withdrawn.

value.zh: 建興元年，為中護軍、征南將軍，封永昌亭侯，遷鎮東將軍。
value.en: In Jianxing 1 (223) he became central protector of the army and general who conquers the south, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongchang precinct, and rose to general who guards the east.
value.literal: In the first year of Jianxing he became Central Protector of the Army and General Who Conquers the South, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongchang precinct, and was transferred to General Who Guards the East.

value.zh: 五年，隨諸葛亮駐漢中。
value.en: In the fifth year he followed Zhuge Liang to garrison Hanzhong.
value.literal: In the fifth year he followed Zhuge Liang in garrisoning Hanzhong.

value.zh: 明年，亮出軍，揚聲由斜谷道，曹真遣大眾當之。
value.en: The next year Zhuge Liang marched out, loudly declaring the Xie Valley route; Cao Zhen sent a great host to meet him.
value.literal: The next year Liang marched out, publicly declaring he would take the Xie Valley route; Cao Zhen sent a large force to oppose him.

value.zh: 亮令雲與鄧芝往拒，而身攻祁山。
value.en: Zhuge Liang sent Zhao Yun and Deng Zhi to hold the line while he struck Qishan himself.
value.literal: Liang ordered Yun and Deng Zhi to go resist while he himself attacked Mount Qi.

value.zh: 雲、芝兵弱敵強，失利於箕谷，然斂眾固守，不至大敗。
value.en: Zhao Yun and Deng Zhi were outmatched and lost at Jigu, yet gathered their men, held firm, and escaped catastrophe.
value.literal: Yun and Zhi's troops were weak and the enemy strong; they met defeat at Jigu, yet gathered the force and held firm without suffering great defeat.

value.zh: 軍退，貶為鎮軍將軍。
value.en: After the withdrawal he was demoted to general who guards the army.
value.literal: When the army withdrew, he was demoted to General Who Guards the Army.

value.zh: 雲別傳曰：亮曰：「街亭軍退，兵將不復相錄，箕穀軍退，兵將初不相失，何故？」
value.en: The Zhao Yun biezhuan records Zhuge Liang saying, "At Jieting the army broke and officers and men could not find one another; at Jigu the army withdrew yet officers and men never lost one another—why?"
value.literal: The Zhao Yun biezhuan states: Liang said, "When the Jieting army withdrew, soldiers and generals could no longer find one another; when the Jigu army withdrew, soldiers and generals at first did not lose one another—why?"

value.zh: 芝答曰：「雲身自斷後，軍資什物，略無所棄，兵將無緣相失。」
value.en: Deng Zhi answered, "Zhao Yun covered the retreat himself; stores and gear were scarcely abandoned—officers and men had no chance to lose one another."
value.literal: Zhi answered, "Yun personally covered the retreat; army supplies and goods were almost nothing abandoned—soldiers and generals had no occasion to lose one another."

value.zh: 雲有軍資餘絹，亮使分賜將士，雲曰：「軍事無利，何為有賜？
value.en: Zhao Yun still held surplus army silk; Zhuge Liang had it divided among the officers and soldiers. Zhao Yun said, "The campaign brought no gain—why grant gifts?
value.literal: Yun had surplus silk from army supplies; Liang had it divided and granted to officers and soldiers. Yun said, "The military campaign brought no gain—why should there be gifts?

value.zh: 其物請悉入赤岸府庫，須十月為冬賜。」
value.en: Put it all in the Chian treasury and hold it for the winter grant in the tenth month."
value.literal: Please put all these goods into the Chian office storehouses and wait until the tenth month for the winter grant."

value.zh: 亮大善之。
value.en: Zhuge Liang greatly approved.
value.literal: Liang greatly approved of this.

value.zh: 許靖字文休，汝南平輿人。
value.en: Xu Jing, styled Wenxiu, came from Pingyu in Runan commandery.
value.literal: Xu Jing, courtesy name Wenxiu, was a man of Pingyu in Runan.

value.zh: 少與從弟劭俱知名，並有人倫臧否之稱，而私情不協。
value.en: As a young man he and his cousin Xu Shao rose to fame together, and both were celebrated for sizing up men of the age, yet the two never got along in private.
value.literal: In youth he and his younger cousin Shao were both famous, and together they had a reputation for judging men and ranking character, but in private feeling they were not harmonious.

value.zh: 劭為郡功曹，排擯靖不得齒敘，以馬磨自給。
value.en: When Shao served as the commandery’s merit assessor, he shut Xu Jing out of official placement altogether, and Xu was reduced to earning a living at a horse-driven mill.
value.literal: Shao became merit assessor of the commandery, excluded Jing so that he could not be ranked in order, and Jing supported himself by grinding grain with a horse mill.

value.zh: 颍川劉翊為汝南太守，乃舉靖計吏，察孝廉，除尚書郎，典選舉。
value.en: Liu Yi of Yingchuan, as grand warden of Runan, nominated Xu Jing as accounts clerk, then recommended him on the filial-and-incorrupt roll; Xu was appointed gentleman of the Secretariat and given charge of personnel appointments.
value.literal: Liu Yi of Yingchuan became grand warden of Runan, thereupon recommended Jing as clerk on the annual accounts, investigated him as filial and incorrupt, appointed him gentleman of the masters of writing, and put him in charge of selections.

value.zh: 靈帝崩，董卓秉政，以漢陽周毖為吏部尚書，與靖共謀議，進退天下之士，沙汰穢濁，顯拔幽滯。
value.en: After Emperor Ling’s death, Dong Zhuo took power. He named Zhou Bi of Hanyang director of personnel and had him work with Xu Jing to decide promotions and dismissals across the empire—purging the corrupt and raising men who had long languished in obscurity.
value.literal: When Emperor Ling died, Dong Zhuo seized government, appointed Zhou Bi of Hanyang as director of the Ministry of Personnel, and with Jing together deliberated, advancing and retiring the gentlemen of the realm, washing away the foul and turbid, and manifestly elevating the secluded and blocked.

value.zh: 進用颍川荀爽、韓融、陳紀等為公、卿、郡守，拜尚書韓馥為冀州牧，侍中劉岱為兗州剌史，颍川張咨為南陽太守，陳留孔伷為豫州剌史，東郡張邈為陳留太守，而遷靖巴郡太守，不就，補御史中丞。
value.en: They brought in men such as Xun Shuang, Han Rong, and Chen Ji of Yingchuan to fill the highest civil posts and commandery governorships; Han Fu was made shepherd of Ji, Liu Dai inspector of Yan, Zhang Zi grand warden of Nanyang, Kong Zhou inspector of Yu, and Zhang Miao grand warden of Chenliu. Xu Jing was slated for Ba commandery, but he declined the post and was appointed assistant secretary of the imperial censorate instead.
value.literal: They advanced and employed Xun Shuang, Han Rong, Chen Ji, and others of Yingchuan as dukes, ministers, and grand wardens; invested Masters of Writing Han Fu as shepherd of Ji province, Palace Attendant Liu Dai as inspector of Yan province, Zhang Zi of Yingchuan as grand warden of Nanyang, Kong Zhou of Chenliu as inspector of Yu province, Zhang Miao of Dong commandery as grand warden of Chenliu; and transferred Jing to be grand warden of Ba commandery, but he did not take up the post, and was instead supplemented as palace assistant secretary.

value.zh: 馥等到官，各舉兵還向京都，欲以誅卓。
value.en: Once Han Fu and his colleagues reached their assignments, they each mobilized forces and marched on the capital, aiming to destroy Dong Zhuo.
value.literal: When Fu and the others reached their posts, each raised troops and turned back toward the capital, intending thereby to execute Zhuo.

value.zh: 卓怒毖曰︰「諸君言當拔用善士，卓從諸君計，不欲違天下人心。
value.en: Dong Zhuo rounded on Zhou Bi in fury: "You insisted we elevate worthy men. I followed your counsel because I would not set myself against the will of the realm.
value.literal: Zhuo angrily said to Bi: "You gentlemen said one ought to promote and employ good gentlemen; Zhuo followed your gentlemen's plan and did not wish to go against the hearts of men under Heaven.

value.zh: 而諸君所用人，至官之日，還來相圖。
value.en: Yet the very men you placed in office turned their armies against me the moment they took up their posts.
value.literal: Yet as for the men your gentlemen employed, on the day they reached office, they returned to plot against me.

value.zh: 卓何用查負！」
value.en: What have I done to deserve such treachery in return?"
value.literal: What use has Zhuo for being betrayed!"

value.zh: 叱毖令出，于外斬之。
value.en: He had Zhou Bi hustled outside and executed him on the spot.
value.literal: He shouted at Bi ordering him out, and outside beheaded him.

value.zh: 靖從兄陳相玚，又與伷合規，靖懼誅，奔伷。
value.en: Xu Jing’s cousin Xu Yang, who was chancellor of Chen, was also in league with Kong Zhou’s designs; fearing he would be put to death, Xu Jing fled to Kong Zhou’s camp.
value.literal: Jing's elder cousin Yang, chancellor of Chen, again with Zhou joined in plotting; Jing feared execution and fled to Zhou.

value.zh: 〈蜀記雲：靖後自表曰：「黨賊求生，情所不忍；
value.en: 〈The Shu Ji records that Xu Jing later explained in a memorial: "To side with rebels merely to save my skin was more than conscience would allow;
value.literal: 〈The Shu Ji states: Later Jing himself in a memorial said: "To cling to rebels to seek life, in feeling is what I cannot bear;

value.zh: 守官自危，死不成義。
value.en: to cling to an empty title while peril closed in would have been a death that accomplished no duty worth the name.
value.literal: to guard office and endanger oneself, to die and not complete righteousness.

value.zh: 竊念古人當難詭常，權以濟其道。」〉
value.en: I recalled how the ancients, in extremity, bent the usual rules and used timely shifts of course to preserve what truly mattered."〉
value.literal: I privately thought that the ancients, facing difficulty, altered the constant, and by expediency aided their way."〉

value.zh: 伷卒，依揚州剌史陳祎。
value.en: After Kong Zhou died, Xu Jing took refuge with Chen Yi, the inspector of Yang province.
value.literal: When Zhou died, he relied on Chen Yi, inspector of Yang province.

value.zh: 祎死，吳郡都尉許貢、會稽太守王朗素與靖有舊，故往保焉。
value.en: When Chen Yi died, Wu’s commandant Xu Gong and Kuaiji’s grand warden Wang Lang—both old acquaintances—offered Xu Jing shelter.
value.literal: When Yi died, Commandant of Wu Commandery Xu Gong and Grand Warden of Kuaiji Wang Lang, who from old had ties with Jing, therefore went to protect there.

value.zh: 靖收恤親裡，經紀振贍，出于仁濃。
value.en: Xu Jing gathered his kinsmen and neighbors, organized relief, and kept them fed—acts born of deep human kindness.
value.literal: Jing gathered and comforted kin and neighborhood, managed and relieved and supported, coming from thick benevolence.

value.zh: 書非史記周圖，仲尼不采，道非虛無自然，嚴平不演。
value.en: Confucius took nothing into the classics that was not grounded in the histories and charts of Zhou; Yan Junping expounded no Way that was not rooted in emptiness and naturalness.
value.literal: Books that are not the historical records of Zhou charts, Zhongni did not gather; the Way that is not empty void self-so, Yan Ping did not expound.

value.zh: 海以受淤，歲一蕩清；
value.en: The sea accepts silt from every stream, yet each year a great tide scours it clean;
value.literal: The sea by receiving silt, each year once washes clear;

value.zh: 君子博識，非禮不視。
value.en: and the gentleman may read widely, but he does not look at what is contrary to ritual.
value.literal: the gentleman's broad knowledge, if not ritual he does not view.

value.zh: 今戰國反覆儀、秦之術，殺人自生，亡人自存，經之所疾。
value.en: The Intrigues teach the shifting schemes of Su Qin and Zhang Yi—killing others to save oneself, ruining others to survive. The classics condemn such things.
value.literal: Now the Warring States turn and return the arts of Yi and Qin, kill others to live oneself, destroy others to preserve oneself; the classics abhor this.

value.zh: 故孔子發憤作《春秋》。
value.en: That is why Confucius, in indignation, composed the Chunqiu.
value.literal: Therefore Kongzi in wrath composed the Spring and Autumn.

value.zh: 大乎居正，複製《孝經》，廣陳德行。
value.en: How great is the principle of holding to the right! He also composed the Classic of Filial Piety to set forth virtue in breadth.
value.literal: Great is dwelling in rectitude; again he made the Classic of Filial Piety, broadly set forth virtue and conduct.

value.zh: 杜漸防萌，預有所抑，是以老氏絕禍于未萌，豈不信邪﹗成湯大聖，睹野魚而有獵逐之失，定公賢者，見女樂而棄朝事，
value.en: He checked evil in its first stirrings and curbed excess before it could grow—hence Laozi cuts off calamity before it buds; can you doubt it? Tang the Completer was a great sage, yet the sight of wild game led him to hunting excess; Duke Ding of Lu was a worthy ruler, yet the sight of female musicians made him neglect court business;
value.literal: Stop gradual prevent sprouting, beforehand have what to restrain; therefore the Old Master cut off disaster before not sprouting, is it not trustworthy! Cheng Tang great sage, seeing wild fish yet had hunting pursuit's fault; Duke Ding worthy man, seeing women's music then abandoned court affairs,

value.zh: 〈臣松之案：書傳魯定公無善可稱。
value.en: 〈Pei Songzhi notes: the transmitted texts record no virtue in Duke Ding of Lu worth praising.
value.literal: 〈Your subject Songzhi investigates: in documents and transmissions Duke Ding of Lu has no good worth praising.

value.zh: 宓謂之賢者，淺學所未達也。〉
value.en: For Qin Mi to call him a worthy shows a shallow reading of the sources.
value.literal: Mi calling him worthy man, shallow learning has not reached.

value.zh: 若此輩類，焉可勝陳。
value.en: Examples of this sort could fill many pages.
value.literal: If this sort of kind, how can they be fully arrayed.

value.zh: 道家法曰︰‘不見所欲，使心不亂。
value.en: The Daoist maxim runs, "Give the eye no craving and the heart will not be thrown into turmoil.
value.literal: The Daoist law says: "Not seeing what is desired, causes the mind not to be chaotic.

value.zh: ’是故天地貞觀，日月貞明，其直如矢，君子所覆。
value.en: Hence Heaven and Earth hold to constancy, sun and moon shine with constancy, and the straight course flies like an arrow—such is the model the gentleman embraces."
value.literal: Therefore Heaven and Earth are correct in viewing, sun and moon correct in brightness; their straightness like arrows; what the gentleman covers."

value.zh: 《洪范》記災，發于言貌，何戰國之譎權乎哉﹗
value.en: The Hong fan traces calamity to words and bearing—what have they to do with the cunning stratagems of the Warring States?
value.literal: The Hong Fan records disasters, arising from speech and appearance; what Warring States deceitful stratagems!

value.zh: 黃權，字公衡，巴西閬中人也。
value.en: Huang Quan, styled Gongheng, came from Langzhong in Ba-Xi Commandery.
value.literal: Huang Quan, courtesy name Gongheng, was a man of Langzhong in Ba-Xi.

value.zh: 少為郡吏，州牧劉璋召為主簿。
value.en: He began as a county clerk until Yi Province Governor Liu Zhang named him chief clerk.
value.literal: In youth he was a county clerk; Governor Liu Zhang summoned him as chief clerk.

value.zh: 時別駕張鬆建議，宜迎先主，使伐張魯。
value.en: Zhang Song, Liu Zhang’s vice administrator, urged inviting Liu Bei west to attack Zhang Lu.
value.literal: At that time Vice Administrator Zhang Song proposed that it was fitting to welcome the First Sovereign and send him to campaign against Zhang Lu.

value.zh: 權諫曰：「左將軍有驍名，今請到，欲以部曲遇之，則不滿其心，欲以賓客禮待，則一國不容二君。
value.en: Huang Quan objected: “The Left General is famous as a fighter. Treat him like a subordinate and he will resent it; treat him as an honored guest and two masters cannot share one realm.
value.literal: Quan remonstrated, saying: 'The Left General has a fierce reputation; now if we invite him and wish to treat him as retainers [buqu], we will not satisfy his heart; if we wish to receive him with the rites due a guest, then one state cannot contain two lords.

value.zh: 若容有泰山之安，則主有累卵之危。
value.en: Your guest would stand firm as Taishan while you teeter like a stack of eggs.
value.literal: If the guest has the security of Mount Tai, then the lord has the peril of piled eggs.

value.zh: 可但閉境，以待河清。」
value.en: Better seal the passes and wait until the world settles.”
value.literal: One may simply close the borders and await the river running clear [i.e. peace in the realm].'

value.zh: 璋不聽，竟遣使迎先生，出權為廣漢長，及先主襲取益州，將帥分下郡縣。
value.en: Liu Zhang refused, sent an envoy to welcome Liu Bei anyway, and transferred Huang Quan out as chief of Guanghan. When Liu Bei seized Yi Province by surprise, generals and commanders spread through the commanderies and counties.
value.literal: Zhang did not listen; in the end he dispatched an envoy to welcome the First Sovereign; he transferred Quan out to be chief of Guanghan; when the First Sovereign seized Yi Province by surprise, generals and commanders fanned out into commanderies and counties.

value.zh: 郡縣風景附，權閉城堅守，須劉璋稽服，乃詣降先主。
value.en: County after county yielded; Huang Quan held his walls until Liu Zhang capitulated, then opened his gates to Liu Bei.
value.literal: Commanderies and counties submitted like wind and shadow [swiftly]; Quan closed the city and defended firmly; he waited until Liu Zhang bowed in submission, then went to surrender to the First Sovereign.

value.zh: 先主假權偏將軍。
value.en: Liu Bei named him acting lieutenant general.
value.literal: The First Sovereign appointed Quan acting Lieutenant General.

value.zh: 〈徐眾評曰：權既忠諫於主，又閉城拒守，得事君之禮。
value.en: 〈Xu Zhong remarks that Huang Quan both warned his lord faithfully and held his city—proper conduct for a minister.
value.literal: 〈Xu Zhong appraises: Quan both loyally remonstrated his lord and closed the city and resisted defense—he obtained the rites of serving a lord.

value.zh: 武王下車，封比干之墓，表商容之閭，所以大顯忠賢之士，而明示所貴之旨。
value.en: King Wu honored Bi Gan’s tomb and Shang Rong’s lane to proclaim loyalty—the standard Liu Bei should emulate.
value.literal: When King Wu stepped down from his chariot, he enfeoffed Bi Gan's tomb and marked Shang Rong's lane—thereby greatly displaying loyal and worthy men and clearly showing the aim of what is honored.

value.zh: 先主假權將軍，善矣，然猶薄少，未足彰忠義之高節，而大勸為善者之心。〉
value.en: Promoting him to general was decent but too modest to honor such steadfast loyalty or inspire others.〉
value.literal: That the First Sovereign appointed Quan general is good, yet still meager—it does not suffice to display the lofty integrity of loyalty and righteousness or greatly encourage the hearts of those who do good.〉

value.zh: 及曹公破張魯，魯走入巴中，權進曰：「若失漢中，則三巴不振，此為割蜀之股臂也。」
value.en: When Cao Cao drove Zhang Lu into Bazhong, Huang Quan urged: “Lose Hanzhong and the Three Ba collapse—you would sever Shu’s limbs.”
value.literal: When Duke Cao defeated Zhang Lu, Lu fled into Ba-Zhong; Quan advanced his view, saying: 'If we lose Hanzhong, then the Three Ba will not flourish—this is cutting off Shu's thigh and arm.'

value.zh: 於是先主以權為護軍，率諸將迎魯，魯已還南鄭，北降曹公。
value.en: Liu Bei made Huang Quan protector of the army and marched to intercept Zhang Lu, but Zhang Lu had already doubled back to Nan Zheng and surrendered to Cao Cao.
value.literal: Thereupon the First Sovereign appointed Quan Protector of the Army and led the various generals to welcome Lu; Lu had already returned to Nan Zheng and submitted north to Duke Cao.

value.zh: 然卒破杜濩、樸胡，殺夏候淵，據漢中，皆權本謀也。
value.en: Yet the victories over Du Hu and Pu Hu, the death of Xiahou Yuan, and the seizure of Hanzhong all stemmed from Huang Quan’s original plan.
value.literal: Yet in the end [they] defeated Du Hu and Pu Hu, killed Xiahou Yuan, and occupied Hanzhong—all were Quan's original stratagem.

value.zh: 初，平同郡漢昌句
value.en: Wang Ping had a fellow townsman from Hanchang surnamed Gou—
value.literal: At first, [there was one] Gou of Hanchang in the same commandery as Ping—

value.zh: 〈句古候反〉
value.en: 〈Here the surname Gou is read like English "go" (the fanqie gloss gives an ancient hou reading), not like "jyu."〉
value.literal: 〈The surname Gou is read gou (ancient hou fan cut).〉

value.zh: 忠勇寬厚，數有戰功，功名爵位亞平，官至左將軍，封宕渠侯。
value.en: —named Gou Fu—who was loyal, brave, generous, and substantial, repeatedly won battle merit, stood second only to Wang Ping in achievement, fame, rank, and title, rose to Left General, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Dangqu.
value.literal: —loyal, brave, generous, and thick—several times meritorious in battle; his merit, fame, rank, and titles stood second to Ping; he reached Left General and was enfeoffed Marquis of Dangqu.

value.zh: 〈《華陽國志》曰：後張翼、廖化並為大將軍，時人語曰：「前有王、句，後有張、廖。」〉
value.en: 〈Chang Qu notes that when Zhang Yi and Liao Hua became grand generals, folk rhymed: “Wang and Gou led the way; Zhang and Liao followed.”〉
value.literal: 〈The Records of Huayang states: Later Zhang Yi and Liao Hua both became Grand Generals; people of the time said: "Before there were Wang and Gou; after there are Zhang and Liao."〉

value.zh: 在郡十五年，邦域安穆。
value.en: Fifteen quiet years in Yuexi.
value.literal: Fifteen years in the commandery—the domain was secure and calm.

value.zh: 屢乞求還，乃徵詣成都。
value.en: He begged recall until Chengdu summoned him.
value.literal: Repeatedly begging to return, he was at last summoned to Chengdu.

value.zh: 夷民戀慕，扶轂泣涕，過旄牛邑，邑君襁負來迎，及追尋至蜀郡界，其督相率隨嶷朝貢者百餘人。
value.en: Tribes clung to his wheels, infants met him at Maoniu, and a hundred chiefs escorted him toward Chengdu.
value.literal: Yi commoners clung to him, supporting his carriage hubs and weeping; passing Maoniu town the town lord carried infants to greet him; chasing all the way to Shu Commandery border, more than a hundred chiefs followed Ni to court tribute.

value.zh: 嶷至，拜蕩寇將軍，慷慨壯烈，士人咸多貴之。
value.en: Chengdu named him general who sweeps away bandits; literati admired his fire.
value.literal: When Ni arrived he was appointed General Who Sweeps Away Bandits—spirited and heroic—gentlemen all esteemed him.

value.zh: 然放蕩少禮，人亦以此譏焉，
value.en: His blunt manners drew ridicule.
value.literal: Yet he was unrestrained and short on ritual—people also mocked him for this.

value.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：時車騎將軍夏侯霸謂嶷曰：「雖與足下疏闊，然託心如舊，宜明此意。」
value.en: 〈The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: At that time General of Chariots and Cavalry Xiahou Ba said to Zhang Ni, "Although you and I have had little contact, I entrust my heart to you as if we were old friends. You should understand this intention clearly."
value.literal: 〈The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: At that time General of Chariots and Cavalry Xiahou Ba said to Ni: "Although with you, sir, I am distant and broad, yet my heart entrusts as of old—you ought clarify this intent."

value.zh: 嶷答曰：「僕未知子，子未知我，大道在彼，何云託心乎！
value.en: Zhang Ni answered coldly: "We hardly know each other—talk of hearts is premature.
value.literal: Ni replied: "Your servant does not know you, sir; you do not know me—the great Way lies yonder—what speak of entrusting hearts!

value.zh: 原三年之後徐陳斯言。」
value.en: Let three years pass before such intimacy."
value.literal: I beg after three years slowly to state these words."

value.zh: 有識之士以為美談。〉
value.en: Thoughtful men praised the exchange.〉
value.literal: Men of discernment considered this fine conversation.〉

value.zh: 是歲延熙十七年也。
value.en: It was 254.
value.literal: That year was the seventeenth year of Yanxi [254].

value.zh: 魏狄道長李簡密書請降，衛將軍姜維率嶷等因簡之資以出隴西。
value.en: Didao magistrate Li Jian plotted defection; Jiang Wei exploited it to march into Longxi with Zhang Ni.
value.literal: Wei Didao county chief Li Jian secretly wrote requesting surrender; Guard General Jiang Wei led Ni and others using Jian's resources to issue forth into Longxi.

value.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：嶷風濕固疾，至都浸篤，扶杖然後能起。
value.en: 〈Chronic rheumatism crippled him in Chengdu.
value.literal: 〈The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: Ni's rheumatic ailment was chronic; reaching the capital it worsened—only with a staff could he rise.

value.zh: 李簡請降，眾議狐疑，而嶷曰必然。
value.en: Court skeptics doubted Li Jian; Zhang Ni insisted it was genuine.
value.literal: When Li Jian sought surrender the assembly doubted; Ni said it was certain.

value.zh: 姜維之出，時論以嶷初還，股疾不能在行中，由是嶷自乞肆力中原，致身敵庭。
value.en: Though ill from travel he volunteered for Jiang Wei's western thrust anyway.
value.literal: When Jiang Wei marched forth, contemporary opinion held that Ni had just returned and leg ailment kept him from the column—thereby Ni himself begged to exert strength in the Central Plains and give his body to the enemy court.

value.zh: 臨發，辭後主曰：「臣當值聖明，受恩過量，加以疾病在身，常恐一朝隕沒，辜負榮遇。
value.en: Before marching he told Liu Shan: “I have enjoyed imperial favor beyond merit and bear a sickly frame—I dread dying overnight and failing your trust.
value.literal: As he was about to set out, taking leave of the Later Lord he said: 'Your servant has encountered sagely clarity and received favor beyond measure; added to that sickness afflicts my body—I constantly fear falling dead one morning and betraying this splendid encounter.

value.zh: 天不違原，得豫戎事。
value.en: Heaven granted my wish to join the campaign.
value.literal: Heaven did not thwart my prayer; I was able to take part in martial affairs.

value.zh: 若涼州克定，臣為籓表守將；
value.en: If we secure Liangzhou I will hold the frontier for you;
value.literal: If Liangzhou is conquered and settled, your servant will be a frontier-screen guarding commander on the outer defense;

value.zh: 若有未捷，殺身以報。」
value.en: if not, I give my life in repayment.”
value.literal: If there is no victory, I will kill myself to repay.'

value.zh: 後主慨然為之流涕。〉
value.en: Liu Shan wept at his words.〉
value.literal: The Later Lord sighed deeply and for him shed tears.〉

value.zh: 既到狄道，簡悉率城中吏民出迎軍。
value.en: At Didao, Li Jian brought the whole town out to greet Jiang Wei’s host.
value.literal: When they reached Didao, Jian led all clerks and commoners of the city out to welcome the army.

value.zh: 軍前與魏將徐質交鋒，嶷臨陣隕身，然其所殺傷亦過倍。
value.en: He fought Xu Zhi at the front and died in action after inflicting more than twice his own losses.
value.literal: Before the army he crossed blades with Wei general Xu Zhi; Ni fell in facing battle—yet those he killed and wounded were also more than double.

value.zh: 既亡，封長子瑛西鄉侯，次子護雄襲爵。
value.en: After he died, his eldest son Ying was enfeoffed as marquis of Xixiang and his second son Huguo inherited the noble title.
value.literal: After his death, his eldest son Ying was enfeoffed Marquis of Xixiang; second son Huguo succeeded to the noble rank.
